Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - Live-test whether the agent and the connect-moonraker skill guide adding the user's Moonraker printer. Done twice: the Docker Moonraker, then the real Pi at `http://raspberrypi.local/`.
   - Fix offers were declined: "Not now".
   - Test whether the Home printer card works as specified on the JusPrin v2 canvas. Done and reported.
   - "create a task chip to find out the reason why the skill file didn't do good enough job…": a session was started; its diagnosis is done.
   - "why did you pause it. continue": the card test was continued and finished.
   - **Current request:** "is the card wrong because of a bug? This sounds like a thought that's just too stupid to be made by an agent. Find out why the bug was there so that we can fix all similar bugs instead of just fixing one by one as we discovered it."

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - JusPrin, a fork of OrcaSlicer. HomeUI is a React page in a wxWebView, talking to the app over the `jusprin-home-bridge` protocol.
   - `HomeSnapshot` / `PrinterEntry` hold the printer data. `OrcaHomeBackend` builds the cards.
   - `PrinterChip` is the collapsed card and `PrinterCard` the expanded one.
   - Moonraker host polling: `HostLaneReader` and `HostStatus`, with `HostLink` Checking / Reachable / Unreachable. Poll every 10 s; a reading stays fresh for 30 s.
   - Skills live in `AgentUI/src/skills/*/SKILL.md`.
   - Request log: `datadir/jusprin/request-log/*.json`.
   - Dev page overrides: `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` and `JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL`. `JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9/v1` blocks model calls.
   - The canvas artifact: board files are `project/*.dc.html` and components are imported with `dc-import`.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/HomeSnapshot.hpp:70,103`:
     - `enum class PrinterState { Idle, Printing, Offline };`
     - `PrinterState state{PrinterState::Idle};`
     - Both added in c346a5348e (2026-09-12). There is no "unknown" value.
   - `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp`:
     - The only place state is set is `describe_device(MachineObject&, PrinterEntry&)` at lines 140–168, for Bambu machines only:
       `printer.state = !connected ? Offline : printing ? Printing : Idle;`
     - Here `printing = MachineObject::is_in_printing_status(machine.print_status)`.
     - The named-printer loop (about lines 320–390) never sets state for a print host. With `print_host` saved, `connection_state` is set to `Connected`. Then `host_status`: Reachable keeps Connected, Unreachable gives Offline plus reconnect, otherwise "Checking connection…".
   - `HomeUI/src/components/PrinterCard.tsx`, in `PrinterChip`:
     - `idle = printer.state === 'idle' && (connectionState === 'online' || 'connected')`, and then it shows "Idle" with a dot.
     - Added in dbec3e3a38 (2026-10-26, "Home v3 page").
     - In `PrinterCard`, `DOT_LABEL` is green for online or connected.
   - `HomeUI/src/App.tsx`: `startsCollapsed = state !== 'printing' && connectionAction !== 'reconnect'`.
   - Commit 3b3e1ea36a (2026-09-25), "Give every Home printer card one shape, each line verified":
     - Introduced the Connection, Model and Loaded rows.
     - Set the principle that each line rests on something the host verified.
     - For print hosts, "Connected · <address>" was shown once an address was saved.
   - Commit 1e501a9cbe (2026-09-27) added the Moonraker host_status reachability check.
   - Read, not edited:
     - `AgentUI/src/skills/connect-moonraker/SKILL.md`
     - `Printers/HostLanes.hpp`
     - `Printers/NamedPrinters.cpp` (`named_printers()`)
     - `resources/profiles/Custom/machine/MyKlipper 0.4 nozzle.json` (printable_area 250×250, height 250)
   - Canvas boards read into `scratchpad/artifact-files/6c3cbfd4-…/project/`:
     - `comp-printer-card` collapsed idle: height 42, padding 10/12, grey dot, "Idle".
     - `comp-printer-card` expanded printing: camera, header dot, job plus progress, one specs line, filament row, Launch monitor.
     - `credits-08d` and `history-05` idle cards: an "Idle" line, a specs line, a print-history link, and a hollow dot ring.
   - Memory written: `kenneth-real-moonraker-raspberrypi-local.md`. MEMORY.md compacted to 132 lines; a backup is in scratchpad as `MEMORY.md.bak`.
   - Report folder `scratchpad/report/`:
     - `moonraker-live-chat.md`, `raspberrypi-live-chat.md`
     - `home-after.jpg`
     - `card-1-chip-idle.jpg` through `card-6-reconnect-chat.jpg`

4. Errors and fixes:
   - Background clicks failed because the window was off-Space and the user was in a full-screen app. Fixed by serving an instrumented Home page through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL`, with JS clicks done by a long-poll command loop on a local server at 127.0.0.1:8799.
   - `sleep` chains were blocked by the harness; used until-loops instead.
   - `--include` globs failed in zsh; used plain directory paths instead.
   - Artifact read with `paths` plus `prompt` was refused; removed `prompt`.
   - User feedback: they asked why I paused the card test. I had ended the turn because the start_session tool said to. The user wanted the test to continue, so I continued it.

5. Problem Solving:
   - **Root cause found so far:**
     - The state field's default `Idle` doubles as "nothing known".
     - Only Bambu devices ever set state.
     - The enum has no Unknown value.

input.recap: The Home card says "Idle" for your Moonraker printer because the Home printer record has no way to say "state not known". Its state field starts as Idle, and only Bambu printers ever overwrite it. Only Home has this flaw; nothing is fixed yet.
input.ask: Should I add an "unknown" state so the card stops claiming Idle?

content.text:
Yes, it's a bug, and two separate mistakes made it. The first one sat harmless for six weeks until the second one exposed it.

**How it happened**

1. **Mid-September (c346a5348e):** the first Home page added a printer-state field with three values: Idle, Printing and Offline. There is no "not known" value, and every record starts as Idle (`Home/HomeSnapshot.hpp:103`). Only the Bambu code path ever sets the field (`Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:144`). That commit was tested against a fake Bambu A1 mini only. Back then no screen showed the state as text, so nobody saw that a Moonraker printer's "Idle" was just the starting value.
2. **Late October (dbec3e3a38, "Home v3"):** the one-line collapsed card was added. It shows "Idle" whenever the state reads idle and the connection reads connected. For a Moonraker host, "connected" only means the server answered in the last 30 seconds. Nobody asks Klipper what it is doing. So your printer showed "Idle" while Klipper was shut down with a lost MCU.

The page's data type says every printer has one of those three states. The person writing the card trusted that type, which looked reasonable. The tests couldn't catch it: the test fixture starts every printer as `state: 'idle'`, and no test covers the collapsed card for a print-host printer.

The general mistake is a field that can't say "not known", whose starting value already claims something, and that only one kind of printer fills in. Readers can't tell a real reading from the starting value.

**Is it anywhere else?** I searched the fork's code for fields that start out claiming something good, and for every place that turns printer state into words.
- **Only Home has it.** It is the only field in the fork that starts out claiming something good.
- **The top-bar printer chip gets it right.** Its state type has an explicit `NotConnected` value, commented as "a host Orca does not report state for" (`Shell/SetupCommands.hpp:108`).
- **The "other printers" rows in that menu also get it right.** They say "Connected" for a host, not "Idle", and a comment there warns about exactly this mistake (`Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp:152`). They read Home's connection reading, not its state field.
- **The agent's printer list gets it right.** It leaves activity empty for a Moonraker printer, so the model is never told "idle".

There is one related weak spot, which is a judgment call rather than the same bug. OctoPrint, PrusaLink and other non-Moonraker hosts get a green "Connected · address" just because an address is saved. Nothing ever checks them again. A code comment calls part of this "an accepted gap".

**Proposed fix (not agreed yet).** Add an "unknown" value as the starting state and teach the page's type about it. Then the compiler makes every reader decide what unknown looks like, instead of each bug being found one at a time. The collapsed card would show the connection line ("Connected · raspberrypi.local") and stop claiming Idle. I would add a test for a Moonraker printer's collapsed card that fails before the change. All of this is in fork-owned files. The bug is already reproduced: it was on screen during today's card test.

A bigger option is to also read Klipper's own state from Moonraker, so the card can truthfully say Idle, Printing, Paused or Error. Moonraker reports this, and the app already polls the same server every 10 seconds. I haven't checked how much work that is.

**Still open:** I haven't checked whether a paused or failed Bambu printer also reads as Idle. That depends on Orca's `is_in_printing_status`.
So you did investigation only on the printer status, right? No other parts of the printer cards, right?

Mostly yes. I traced two lines on the card: the state word ("Idle") and the connection line ("Connected · address"). I did not audit the card's other parts for the same kind of mistake, which is a starting value or an old reading shown as a current fact.

Here is what I did cover:
- **The state word.** I found the root cause: it starts as Idle, and only Bambu printers ever set it.
- **The connection line.** OctoPrint and other non-Moonraker hosts get a green "Connected" just because an address is saved, and nothing checks them again.
- **A search across the whole fork.** I looked for fields that start out claiming something good, like Idle, Ready, Online, Connected or Verified, or true. It matched on field names like state, status and connected, so a field with another name could slip past.
- **Other places that show printer state.** The top-bar printer chip, the "other printers" rows in its menu, and the agent's printer list all handle "not known" correctly.

I did not check these card parts:
- **The Model row** ("X1 Carbon · 0.4 mm"). It comes from the profile, but a Bambu printer's reported nozzle can replace it. I didn't check what a Moonraker card shows when the profile and the hardware disagree.
- **The Loaded row.** For Moonraker it shows the last reading from the multi-filament unit. I didn't check whether an old reading stays on screen after the host goes quiet.
- **The print-history line** and its "Print again" readiness.
- **The buttons.** These are Launch monitor and Open printer window: for a print host, Open printer window is offered once an address is saved, without checking that the host answers. Reconnect, and the menu actions (settings, rename, remove), aren't checked either.
- **The expanded printing card.** That's the camera, job name, progress bar and specs line. A Moonraker printer never reaches it, because its state is never set to Printing.

Checking those means reading where each line's value comes from and whether a starting or old value can show up as current. It's code reading, so I'd expect it to take about the same time as the state investigation. No live-model calls are needed. Say if you want me to do it; I'd report it the same way, with each line marked as verified or inferred.

input.name: monitor-investigation
input.prompt:
Investigate why the monitor button on JusPrin's Home printer card, and the monitor screen it opens, don't work as Kenneth expects. Find the root cause, and say whether it belongs to a class of similar bugs. Don't just patch one symptom.

What the code does today, as far as I know (verify it yourself):
- On the Home page, a printer card offers "Launch monitor" for a Bambu printer and "Open printer window" for a print host such as Moonraker or OctoPrint.
- The button is offered when `can_launch_monitor` is true. For a print host, `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp` (the named-printer loop, around lines 330–365) sets that flag as soon as a `print_host` address is saved. <result>I found state lists for most of the APIs. Three gaps remain. Elegoo's Centauri Carbon codes come from community sources only. Creality K1/K2 has no published state enum. Duet's progress and filament fields are unconfirmed. Everything I could not confirm is marked unverified.

## 1. Bambu Lab MQTT

- **Where it comes from:** The printer publishes on `device/{DEVICE_ID}/report` over TLS port 8883. You can reach it on the LAN (user `bblp` plus the access code) or through `us.mqtt.bambulab.com` ([OpenBambuAPI mqtt.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/mqtt.md)).
- **State field:** `print.gcode_state`. OpenBambuAPI only shows `IDLE` as an example. The ha-bambulab integration accepts `failed, finish, idle, init, offline, pause, prepare, running, slicing, unknown` ([const.py](https://github.com/greghesp/ha-bambulab/blob/main/custom_components/bambu_lab/pybambu/const.py)).
- **Busy detail:** `stg_cur` gives about 78 stage codes, for example 1 auto bed leveling and 2 heatbed preheating. Idle is -1 on X1 and 255 on P1 (same const.py).
- **Cancelled vs. error:** Both end in `FAILED`. A cancel is recognised only because `print_error == 50348044` arrives first ([models.py](https://github.com/greghesp/ha-bambulab/blob/main/custom_components/bambu_lab/pybambu/models.py)).
- **Errors:** Health messages (HMS) carry a severity (fatal, serious, common, info) and a module (mainboard, AMS, toolhead) (const.py).
- **Progress and job:** `mc_percent`, `mc_remaining_time`, `subtask_name`, `gcode_file` ([mqtt.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/mqtt.md)). The time-left unit is unverified.
- **Material:** Each AMS tray reports `tray_type`, `tray_color` (RRGGBBAA) and `remain`. `tray_now` is `ams_id*4 + tray_id`, or 254 for the external spool (mqtt.md).
- **Offline:** MQTT has no field for it; you only see the connection drop. The cloud device list has `online` and `dev_online` ([cloud-http.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/cloud-http.md)). Bambu has no separate "firmware down" state.

## 2. Moonraker / Klipper

- **Firmware state:** `webhooks.state` and `/printer/info` `state` are `ready, startup, shutdown, error` ([Klipper Status Reference](https://www.klipper3d.org/Status_Reference.html), [Moonraker printer API](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/printer/)).
- **Print state:** `print_stats.state` is `standby, printing, paused, complete, cancelled, error` ([print_stats.py](https://github.com/Klipper3d/klipper/blob/master/klippy/extras/print_stats.py)).
- **Busy:** `idle_timeout.state` is `Idle, Printing, Ready`. "Printing" there means busy, so it covers homing and heating too ([Status Reference](https://www.klipper3d.org/Status_Reference.html)).
- **Progress and job:** `virtual_sdcard.progress` (by file position), `display_status.progress` (from M73), `print_stats.filename`, `print_duration`, and `info.current_layer`/`total_layer`. There is no time-left field; you compute it (Status Reference).
- **Material:** Core Klipper only has filament sensors (`filament_detected`). MMU/AFC lane objects are unverified.
- **Firmware down vs. offline:** Moonraker keeps answering while Klipper is down. `/server/info` returns `klippy_connected` and `klippy_state` = `disconnected | startup | ready | error | shutdown` ([server API](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/server/)). Requests to Klipper then fail with HTTP 503 "Klippy Host not connected" ([klippy_connection.py](https://github.com/Arksine/moonraker/blob/master/moonraker/components/klippy_connection.py)). A failed HTTP connection to Moonraker means offline.

## 3. OctoPrint REST

- **Flags:** `/api/printer` `state.flags` has `operational, printing, paused, pausing, cancelling, sdReady, error, ready, closedOrError` ([data model](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/datamodel.html)). The source adds `resuming` and `finishing` ([standard.py](https://github.com/OctoPrint/OctoPrint/blob/master/src/octoprint/printer/standard.py)).
- **State text:** Offline, Opening serial connection, Detecting serial connection, Connecting, Operational, Starting, Printing, Paused, Pausing, Resuming, Finishing, Error, Offline after error, Transferring file to SD, Cancelling ([comm.py](https://github.com/OctoPrint/OctoPrint/blob/master/src/octoprint/util/comm.py)).
- **Finished and cancelled:** No flag stays set after a job ends. They exist only as events: `PrintDone`, `PrintCancelled`, and `PrintFailed` with `reason` = `cancelled | error` ([events](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/events/index.html)).
- **Progress and job:** `/api/job` gives `completion`, `printTimeLeft`, `file` and `filament` length/volume ([data model](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/datamodel.html)). No material lanes are documented.
- **Firmware down vs. offline:** `/api/printer` returns 409 when the printer is not operational ([printer API](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/printer.html)). Together with `closedOrError` and the Offline text, that means "server up, printer down". A failed HTTP connection means the server is offline.

## 4. PrusaLink / Prusa Connect

- **PrusaLink:** `/api/v1/status` `printer.state` is `IDLE, BUSY, PRINTING, PAUSED, FINISHED, STOPPED, ERROR, ATTENTION, READY` ([openapi.yaml](https://github.com/prusa3d/Prusa-Link-Web/blob/master/spec/openapi.yaml)). STOPPED means cancelled; ATTENTION means the printer needs the user.
- **Job:** `/api/v1/job` gives `progress` (%), `time_remaining`, `file.display_name`, and a job state of `PRINTING, PAUSED, FINISHED, STOPPED, ERROR` (openapi.yaml).
- **MMU:** `/info` has only an `mmu` boolean (openapi.yaml).
- **Prusa Connect SDK:** The same nine states ([const.py](https://github.com/prusa3d/Prusa-Connect-SDK-Printer/blob/master/prusa/connect/printer/const.py)). It adds MMU3 with 5 slots and a `SLOT_EVENT`.
- **Offline:** "OFFLINE" in the Connect web page is a connectivity label, not an enum value (unverified). There is no firmware-down signal separate from ERROR.

## 5. Duet RepRapFirmware

- **State field:** `state.status` is `idle, busy, processing, paused, pausing, resuming, cancelling, changingTool, simulating, starting, updating, off, halted, disconnected` ([DSF MachineStatus](https://duet3d.github.io/DuetSoftwareFramework/api/DuetAPI.ObjectModel.MachineStatus.html)).
- **Firmware down and offline:** `halted` means emergency stop. `off` means the input voltage is too low. `disconnected` means DSF has lost the board.
- **Version note:** Older firmware said `printing`; it was later replaced by `processing` ([forum](https://forum.duet3d.com/post/330299)).
- **Not reported:** There is no finished or cancelled state.
- **Unverified:** progress, time left and file name (I expected `job.*` but did not confirm it), and filament or lanes.

## 6. Repetier-Server

- **Fields:** `listPrinter` returns only `active, job, name, online, slug`. `online` is 1 or 0 ([API](https://www.repetier-server.com/manuals/programming/API/index.html)).
- **Not documented:** paused, error and halted states, and progress fields. Unverified.

## 7. Creality K1/K2 (websocket on port 9999)

- **No published enum.** What follows comes from the ha_creality_ws integration ([utils.py](https://github.com/3dg1luk43/ha_creality_ws/blob/main/custom_components/ha_creality_ws/utils.py)).
- **How it derives states:**
  - non-zero `err.errcode` → error
  - `withSelfTest` between 1 and 99 → self-testing
  - with `printFileName` set:
    - `state` 1 → printing
    - `state` 5 → paused
    - `state` 4 → stopped
    - `state` 0, 7 or 9 → processing
  - progress ≥ 100 → completed
- **Progress and job:** `printProgress`, `printLeftTime`, `printFileName`.
- **Material:** CFS slots exist; the field names are unverified.
- **Offline:** detected only by the socket failing.
- **Creality Cloud:** unverified.

## 8. Elegoo SDCP

- **Official spec (resin):** `CurrentStatus` 0 idle, 1 printing, 2 file transfer, 3 exposure test, 4 self-check. `PrintInfo.Status` 0–10: idle, homing, descending, exposing, lifting, pausing, paused, stopping, stopped, completed, file checking ([SDCP V3.0.0](https://github.com/cbd-tech/SDCP-Smart-Device-Control-Protocol-V3.0.0)).
- **Fields:** `Filename`, layers, `CurrentTicks`/`TotalTicks`, `ErrorNumber`. There is no offline state, only a ping/pong heartbeat.
- **Centauri Carbon codes (community):** 0 idle, 1 homing, 5 pausing, 6 paused, 7 stopping, 8 stopped, 9 completed, 13 printing, 14 error, 15 leveling, 16 preheating. On the CC2, 27–29 are filament switch, load and unload ([pycentauri](https://pypi.org/project/pycentauri/)).
- **Centauri Carbon `CurrentStatus` (community):** 3 means calibrating ([OpenCentauri](https://suchmememanyskill.github.io/OpenCentauri/software/api)).

## 9. Flashforge, HTTP on port 8898

- **State field:** `/detail` `status` is `ready, busy, calibrate_doing, heating, printing, pausing, pause, canceling, cancel, completed, error, downloading`. Firmware 5.x adds `cloud_slicing, sending, unzipping`. The docs say to treat unknown values as busy ([wiki](https://github.com/Parallel-7/flashforge-api-docs/wiki/HTTP-REST-API)).
- **Progress and job:** `printProgress` is 0–1, not a percent. `estimatedTime` is time remaining. `printFileName`, `errorCode`.
- **Material:** On the AD5X, `matlStationInfo.slotInfos[]` gives `hasFilament`, `materialName`, `materialColor` and `currentSlot` ([AD5X](https://github.com/Parallel-7/flashforge-api-docs/wiki/AD5X)).

## 10. Others

- **MKS WiFi:** M997 → IDLE, PRINTING or PAUSE; M27 → percent ([Mischianti](https://mischianti.org/mks-wifi-for-makerbase-robin-communication-protocol-and-cura-plugin-3/)).
- **ESP3D:** ESP800 reports capabilities, not print state ([esp3d.io](https://esp3d.io/esp3d/v3.x/documentation/commands/esp800/)).
- **FlashAir:** file upload only. That no state is reported is my inference ([Prusa blog](https://blog.prusa3d.com/easy-wireless-printing-with-flashair-sd-cards_8603/)).
- **AstroBox:** an OctoPrint fork; its local API is unverified ([repo](https://github.com/AstroPrint/AstroBox)).
- **Obico:** OctoPrint-shaped. `state.text` is Operational, G-Code Downloading, Printing, Pausing, Paused, Cancelling or Offline, with OctoPrint flags and progress ([docs](https://www.obico.io/docs/api/websocket/)).
- **SimplyPrint:** `/printers/Get` returns status, job and loaded filament; the enum is unverified ([API page](https://simplyprint.io/features/api)).
- **3DPrinterOS:** has a printer list endpoint; its states are unverified ([v2.1](https://intercom.help/3DPrinterOS/en/articles/13516944-3dprinteros-global-api-calls-v2-1)).
- **Qidi Plus4 / Q1 Pro:** stock Klipper with an adapted Moonraker ([QIDI_PLUS4](https://github.com/QIDITECH/QIDI_PLUS4)).
- **Snapmaker U1:** forks of Klipper, Moonraker and Fluidd ([blog](https://snapmaker.com/blog/snapmaker-u1-firmware-now-on-github)).
- **Snapmaker 2.0:** HTTP on 8080, `status` IDLE or RUNNING; the full enum is unverified ([forum](https://forum.snapmaker.com/t/do-snapmaker-2-0-devices-have-a-webpage/5455)).
- **A ready-made common model:** OctoEverywhere already normalises many of these to `idle, warmingup, printing, paused, resuming, complete, cancelled, error`, plus a material-system object ([docs](https://docs.octoeverywhere.com/plugin-api/printer-status/)).

## Matrix

Y = reported, N = not reported, ev = event only, ? = unverified

| API | Idle | Busy | Print | Pause | Done | Cancel | Err/attn | FW down | Offline detect | Progress | Job | Lanes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bambu | Y | Y (PREPARE, stg_cur) | Y | Y | Y | via print_error | Y (FAILED, HMS) | N | MQTT drop / cloud `online` | Y | Y | Y (AMS) |
| Moonraker | Y | Y (idle_timeout) | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y (shutdown/error/disconnected) | HTTP fail vs. 503 | Y | Y | sensors; lanes ? |
| OctoPrint | Y | Starting/Finishing | Y | Y | ev | ev | Y | Y (closedOrError, 409) | HTTP fail | Y | Y | N |
| PrusaLink/Connect | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y (STOPPED) | Y (ATTENTION) | N | ? | Y | Y | MMU3 5 slots (Connect) |
| Duet | Y | Y (busy, changingTool) | Y | Y | N | N | ? | Y (halted, off) | Y (disconnected) | ? | ? | ? |
| Repetier | ? | ? | `job` | ? | ? | ? | ? | ? | `online` 0/1 | ? | Y | ? |
| Creality K | Y | Y (self-test) | Y | Y | from progress | Y (stopped) | Y | N | socket only | Y | Y | CFS ? |
| Elegoo SDCP | Y | Y (homing, leveling, preheat) | Y | Y | Y | Y (stopped) | Y | N | heartbeat | layers, ticks | Y | CC2 codes only |
| Flashforge | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | N | ? | Y (0–1) | Y | AD5X slots |
| MKS WiFi | Y | N | Y | Y | N | N | N | N | TCP | Y | ? | N |

The card needs two separate questions. "Can we reach the host?" fails when the connection fails. "Is the firmware up?" is answered by Moonraker's `klippy_state`, OctoPrint's `closedOrError` / 409 and Duet's `halted`/`off`/`disconnected`. Only those three report firmware down separately from unreachable.

Finished and cancelled need event or transition tracking on OctoPrint, Bambu and Duet; the others report them as states.</result>

<result>I've traced every connection type through the code. Only Bambu printers give the app a live print state today, and that state reaches the Home card. A printer connected through any other route never reports whether it is printing, how far along it is, or any error. Its Home card shows "Idle" whatever the printer is doing. For a Moonraker host, the app's own polling adds two things: whether the host answers, and which filament its multi-filament unit says is loaded.

Everything below is checked in code unless I mark it as an inference. Paths are relative to `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/slic3r/`.

## 1. Bambu (LAN or cloud), through the Bambu network plug-in

**How it's chosen.** If the printer profile's vendor is Bambu, `switch_printer_agent` picks the Bambu agent (`GUI/GUI_App.cpp:3582-3587`). When someone connects a printer in the fork's setup, the fork also installs the Bambu agent itself (`GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:396-411`). The printer pushes status over MQTT, and the upstream file `GUI/DeviceManager.cpp:3049-3726` parses it.

**What the parser reads:**
- Print state: `gcode_state` is stored exactly as sent in `print_status` (`DeviceManager.cpp:3185-3186`, `2399-2402`). The code compares against RUNNING, PAUSE, SLICING, PREPARE, IDLE, FINISH and FAILED (`2273-2337`); the header comment also lists INIT (`DeviceManager.hpp:478`).
- What counts as printing: `is_in_printing_status` is true for PAUSE, RUNNING, SLICING and PREPARE, and false for FINISH, FAILED, IDLE, INIT and an empty value (`2301-2310`). `is_in_printing` uses `print_status`; only when that is empty does it fall back to `iot_print_status`, which comes from the cloud device list's `task_status` (`2313-2321`, `DeviceCore/DevManager.cpp:791`). `is_printing_finished` is true for FINISH and FAILED (`2334-2341`).
- Progress and job: `mc_percent` (`3069-3074`, starts at 0, not -1, `550`), `mc_remaining_time`, `subtask_name`, `gcode_file`, `layer_num` and `total_layer_num` (`3090-3235`).
- Errors: `print_error` (`3096`), `mc_print_error_code` (`3086`) and `hms` (`3698`).
- Temperatures: bed through `DevBed::ParseV1_0` (`3286`), nozzle through `ExtderSystemParser` (`3294`), plus `chamber_temper` (`3296`).
- Nozzle: `nozzle_type` and `nozzle_diameter` (`3414-3423`).
- Filament: the AMS trays and the external spool holder through `DevFilaSystemParser` (`3726`).
- Camera: `ipcam` and `xcam` (`3538`, `3611`).

**How often.** As often as the printer pushes. There is no fixed polling interval.

**How "not known" and liveness are represented:**
- `is_connected()` is false when nothing has arrived for 30 s (`DISCONNECT_TIMEOUT`, `DeviceManager.hpp:31`). For a cloud printer it also needs the cloud server to be connected (`DeviceManager.cpp:2428-2443`).
- `m_is_online` comes from the cloud list's `dev_online` (`DevManager.cpp:773`).
- The fork's stricter test, `has_recent_printer_data`, needs at least one push, `is_connected()`, and a message in the last 30 s (`GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterDiscovery.cpp:69-74`).
- In the fork's snapshot (`PrinterSetupTypes.hpp:39-44`), unknown progress is -1, an unknown job is empty, and unknown temperatures are left empty.

**Home card** (`GUI/JusPrin/Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:140-165`):
- State is Offline, Printing or Idle. Printing comes from `is_in_printing_status`, so a paused, preparing or slicing printer shows "Printing". FAILED and FINISH show as Idle.
- Progress is `mc_print_percent`, shown only while printing, with the text "Printing · N% · time left".
- The connection line reads "Online · LAN" or "Online · Cloud". A printer that was verified before and is now silent reads "Offline" with a Reconnect button.
- Spools come from the AMS trays plus the external spool holder, and only while the printer is connected (`PrinterDiscovery.cpp:39-59`, `OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:302-307`).

The fork reads no error fields, no HMS codes, nothing about the camera, and does not tell paused apart from printing. A search of `GUI/JusPrin` outside `Testing/` found no use of `print_error`, `hms`, PAUSE or FAILED.

## 2. The printer-agent layer for other printers (upstream)

**How a printer gets an agent.** For a non-Bambu profile, the agent is the profile's `printer_agent` string (`libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp:829`). If that is empty, it is the Orca agent (`GUI_App.cpp:3588-3594`). The shipped profiles set "crealityprint" 16 times, "qidi" 4 times, "snapmaker" once and "moonraker" once (OpenEYE).

For any non-Bambu agent, `select_machine` builds a `MachineObject` from `print_host` (`GUI_App.cpp:3633-3708`):
- `dev_id` is the host and port.
- The connection type is "lan" and the bind state is "free".
- The access code is the API key, or "88888888" when there is none.

**Orca agent.** Every call is a stub that reports success, including `connect_printer` (`Utils/OrcaPrinterAgent.cpp:29-32`). It reads nothing.

**Moonraker agent** (Qidi, Snapmaker and Creality build on it):
- On connect it calls GET `/server/info` once, in the background (`MoonrakerPrinterAgent.cpp:1130`, `2052-2083`).
- The first status query and the websocket status stream are switched off with `#if 0` (`2085-2099`; upstream commit 722d5f8aa7, which is on `upstream/main`). So in practice it pushes nothing, the `MachineObject` never gets a message, and `is_in_printing` never becomes true.
- If that code were switched back on:
  - It would subscribe to `print_stats`, `virtual_sdcard`, `heater_bed`, `display_status` and the extruders (`1497-1533`).
  - It would send at most one update per second (`MoonrakerPrinterAgent.hpp:202`), plus a heartbeat every 10 s (`1559`).
  - The state mapping is printing→RUNNING, paused→PAUSE, complete→FINISH, error or cancelled→FAILED, and anything else, including standby, →IDLE (`73-89`).
  - Klippy shutting down or disconnecting would be reported as "error" (`1653-1667`).
  - Progress would come from `virtual_sdcard.progress`, the job from `print_stats.filename`, and temperatures from `extruder` and `heater_bed` (`1804-1874`).
  - Errors would always be sent as 0 (`1771-1775`).
  - It would reach the `MachineObject` through the same parser as Bambu (`1916-1940`).
- Filament is read only when asked (`FilamentSyncMode::pull`), when upstream's filament sync calls it (`GUI/Plater.cpp:3345`). It tries `/server/database/item?namespace=lane_data` first, then `/printer/objects/query?mmu` (`569-597`).
- The subclasses replace only the filament reading:
  - Qidi reads `printer/objects/query?save_variables=variables` and `officiall_filas_list.cfg` (`QidiPrinterAgent.cpp:85`, `214`).
  - Snapmaker reads `printer/objects/query?print_task_config&filament_detect` (`SnapmakerPrinterAgent.cpp:107`).
  - Creality asks for `boxsInfo` over a websocket on port 9999 (`CrealityPrint.cpp:284-298`) and falls back to the Moonraker reading.

**Inference, not run.** The `MachineObject` that `select_machine` creates passes the test for `get_my_machine_list` (LAN, "free", non-empty access code; `DevManager.cpp:663-672`). If so, it would appear on Home as a separate device card. Since it never gets a push, that card would always say Offline.

## 3. Print hosts (upstream adapters)

None of the adapters below has a printer-state query. They only test the connection and upload files. Test endpoints first, then upload:
- **OctoPrint:** test GET `api/version`, reading `api` and `text`. Upload POST `api/files/local`.
- **PrusaLink and PrusaConnect** (same file, `OctoPrint.cpp`): `api/version` plus `upload-by-put`. `get_storage` reads `api/v1/storage` (`name`, `path`, `free_space`, `read_only`, `ro`, `available`; `673-724`).
- **Moonraker:** test `server/info`, which must contain `result.klippy_state` (`Moonraker.cpp:71-90`). Storage list from `server/files/roots`. Upload `server/files/upload`, start with `printer/print/start`.
- **Duet:** `rr_connect` or `machine/status` (`Duet.cpp:203-206`). Upload `rr_upload` or `machine/file`, start with M32 or M37.
- **FlashAir:** `command.cgi?op=118`, upload `upload.cgi`.
- **AstroBox:** `api/version`, upload `api/files/local`.
- **Repetier:** `printer/info` (`name`, `software`). Printer list from `printer/list` (`slug`). Upload `printer/job/<port>` or `printer/model/<port>`.
- **MKS:** sends M105 over TCP. Starts with M23/M24.
- **ESP3D:** `/command?cmd=M105`, upload `/upload_serial`, start with M23/M24.
- **CrealityPrint:** GET `info`, reading `model`. Upload `upload/<file>`.
- **Obico:** `api/v1/version/`. Printer list from `api/v1/printers/` (`name`, `id`). Upload `api/v1/g_code_files/`.
- **Flashforge:** a TCP control command, or the local API `detail` call. That call also gives the material station's slots (`slotId`, `hasFilament`, `materialName`, `materialColor`; `Flashforge.cpp:519-550`), used only in upstream dialogs (`Plater.cpp:16414`, `PrintHostDialogs.cpp:898`).
- **SimplyPrint:** OAuth `oauth2/TokenInfo`, upload `api/files/TempUpload`.
- **ElegooLink:** GET of the base URL, or `system/info?X-Token=` on newer models. When it starts a print, it opens a websocket on port 3030 and waits until `Status.CurrentStatus` no longer contains 8 (`ElegooLink.cpp:1215-1290`). It reads nothing else.
- **3DPrinterOS:** login with a token, `apiglobal/upload`, then `quickprint`.

## 4. The fork's own polling

**Moonraker hosts only.** It reads only named printers whose `host_type` is Moonraker and whose `print_host` is set (`GUI/JusPrin/Printers/HostLaneReader.cpp:120-132`).

**What it reads:**
- GET `server/database/item?namespace=lane_data`, fields `lane`, `material`, `color`.
- Then GET `printer/objects/query?mmu`, fields `num_gates`, `gate_status`, `gate_material`, `gate_color` (`HostLaneReader.cpp:60-80`, `HostLanes.cpp:66-122`).
- Any 200 or 404 reply counts as "the host answered".
- It reads no print state, progress, job, temperature or error.

**How often.** At most every 10 s, and only while Home asks for the readings. A reading counts as fresh for 30 s (`HostLanes.hpp`, `kHostPollInterval`, `kHostReadingFresh`).

**"Not known".** The host state is Checking, Reachable or Unreachable. The loaded-filament list is absent when the host did not say (`HostLanes.cpp:139-155`).

**Testing a host.** The setup's connection test supports only Moonraker and OctoPrint, through `PrintHost::test` (`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:718-765`). Every other host type gets "unavailable". A saved host gets the message "live printer status is not available here" (`478-489`).

**Bambu connection answers.** `ConnectionEvents` records what the Bambu plug-in answered when connecting on the LAN: Ok, Failed or Lost, with the plug-in's code ("5" means a wrong access code). It also probes a TCP port.

## 5. How the readings reach the screens

- **Home, named printer with a print host** (`OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:324-394`):
  - The connection line reads "Connected · <address>". For Moonraker it becomes "Checking connection…" or "Offline", depending on the polling.
  - The state is never set, so it stays at the default, Idle (`HomeSnapshot.hpp:70`). A printer that is mid-print shows Idle.
  - Progress stays -1, so no bar is drawn.
  - Spools are the Moonraker lanes, or nothing.
- **`printer_connection()` (the shell's status row):**
  - For any non-Bambu network it returns NotConnected.
  - For Bambu it uses `is_connected()`, not the stricter `has_recent_printer_data` (`Shell/SetupCommands.cpp:272-296`). For the first moments after connecting, this row can disagree with the Home card.
- **Workspace `printers()`** (what the model sees) covers only machines in the device manager. Activity is printing, idle or offline; it also has progress, job, temperatures and materials (`Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2287-2320`). Printers connected only through a print host don't appear at all.

## Summary table

| Connection | Print state | Progress | Job name | Error / attention | Material loaded | Nozzle | Liveness check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bambu LAN or cloud | read (pause counts as printing) | read | read | read by upstream, not read by the fork | read | read | read (a push within 30 s) |
| Moonraker agent (Klipper, Qidi, Snapmaker, Creality profiles) | not available via this code path (stream switched off) | not available via this code path | not available via this code path | not available via this code path (always 0) | read on request (filament sync) | not available via this code path | `/server/info` once at connect |
| Moonraker host plus the fork's polling | not read | not read | not read | not read | read | not read | read (every 10 s, 30 s window) |
| OctoPrint, PrusaLink, PrusaConnect | not read | not read | not read | not read | not read | not read | test only, on request |
| Flashforge | not read | not read | not read | not read | read in upstream dialogs only | not read | test only |
| Duet, FlashAir, AstroBox, Repetier, MKS, ESP3D, CrealityPrint, Obico, SimplyPrint, ElegooLink, 3DPrinterOS | not read | not read | not read | not read | not read (CrealityPrint: through the agent only) | not read | test only, from upstream's settings dialog; the fork marks them "unavailable" |

**Still open:**
- I haven't confirmed in the running app whether the Moonraker or Orca agent's `MachineObject` really shows up on Home as an extra Offline card.
- I haven't measured how often the Bambu plug-in pushes data.</result>

# Printer states across connection types

Written 2026-11-04. Sections 1 and 2 describe what exists today. Sections 3 to 5 are a proposal that Kenneth has not agreed to.

## 1. What the app reads today, per connection type (verified in code)

| Connection | Print state | Progress / job | Error | Filament loaded | Is it answering? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bambu, LAN or cloud (the Bambu plug-in, over MQTT) | Read. The Home card treats PAUSE, PREPARE and SLICING as "Printing", and FINISH and FAILED as "Idle" (`DeviceManager.cpp:2301`) | Read | Upstream reads it; JusPrin ignores it | Read (AMS and the external spool) | A push within the last 30 s |
| Moonraker (Klipper), through JusPrin's own 10 s poll | Not read | Not read | Not read | Read (`lane_data` or `mmu`) | Read (a reply in the last 30 s) |
| Moonraker, through upstream's printer agent (Qidi, Snapmaker, Creality and OpenEYE profiles) | Code exists but is switched off with `#if 0` upstream, under "disable websocket for now" (`MoonrakerPrinterAgent.cpp:2084`) | Same: switched off | Always 0 | Read only during upstream's filament sync | `/server/info` once, at connect |
| OctoPrint, PrusaLink, PrusaConnect | Not read | Not read | Not read | Not read | Only when someone presses Test |
| Duet, Repetier, MKS, ESP3D, FlashAir, AstroBox, CrealityPrint, Obico, SimplyPrint, ElegooLink, Flashforge, 3DPrinterOS | Not read | Not read | Not read | Flashforge: in upstream dialogs only | Upstream's Test button only; JusPrin's setup calls them "unavailable" |

What the Home card shows today as a result:
- A Bambu card has a real state, but a paused printer reads "Printing", and a failed print reads "Idle".
- Every other card reads "Idle", because that is the state field's starting value. A Moonraker card says whether the host answers. Every other host card says "Connected · address", based only on an address being saved.

## 2. What each printer's own API can report (from its docs or source; "?" = not confirmed)

| API | Ready | Busy (heating, homing, calibrating) | Printing | Paused | Finished / cancelled | Error or needs attention | Controller down while the host still answers | Progress, job name | Filament lanes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bambu MQTT | IDLE | PREPARE, SLICING, `stg_cur` | RUNNING | PAUSE | FINISH; cancel is FAILED + error 50348044 | FAILED, HMS | no such state | yes | AMS |
| Moonraker / Klipper | `print_stats` standby | `idle_timeout` Printing while standby | printing | paused | complete, cancelled | `print_stats` error | `klippy_state` shutdown, error, disconnected | yes; no time left | `mmu`, `lane_data` (sensor only in core Klipper) |
| OctoPrint (also Obico, AstroBox?) | ready | Starting, Finishing, Cancelling, Pausing | printing | paused | events only (`PrintDone`, `PrintCancelled`) | error | `closedOrError`, HTTP 409 | yes | no |
| PrusaLink / Prusa Connect | IDLE, READY | BUSY | PRINTING | PAUSED | FINISHED, STOPPED | ERROR, ATTENTION | no | yes | MMU3 in Connect |
| Duet | idle | busy, changingTool, starting, updating, pausing, resuming, cancelling | processing (older firmware: printing) | paused | no | ? | halted, off, disconnected | ? | ? |
| Flashforge | ready | busy, heating, calibrate_doing, downloading, pausing, canceling | printing | pause | completed, cancel | error | no | yes | AD5X slots |
| Elegoo (Centauri Carbon) | 0 | homing, leveling, preheating | 13 | 6 | 9, 8 | 14 | no | yes | CC2 only |
| Creality K1/K2 (port 9999) | derived | self-test | state 1 | state 5 | progress 100, state 4 | `err.errcode` | no | yes | CFS ? |
| Repetier, MKS, ESP3D, FlashAir, SimplyPrint, 3DPrinterOS | mostly ? or nothing | | | | | | | | |

## 3. Proposed states (proposal)

The card answers two separate questions. Today one field mixes them up.

**Can the app reach it?**
- **Not connected.** No connection is saved.
- **Checking.** The app has asked and has no answer yet.
- **Live.** It answered within the last 30 seconds.
- **Lost.** It answered before and is silent now.
- **Not checked.** An address is saved, but the app never polls this connection type. This replaces today's green "Connected" for OctoPrint and the others.

**What is the printer doing?** This is filled in only while the connection is Live and the connection type reports it. Otherwise it is Unknown, and the card says nothing about activity.
- **Unknown.** This is the starting value.
- **Ready.** Nothing is running, and a job can start.
- **Busy.** The printer is doing something that is not yet a job, such as heating, homing, leveling, self-test or a file transfer.
- **Printing.** Progress, job name and time left come along when the printer reports them.
- **Paused.**
- **Needs attention.** An error the person must deal with. The printer's own message goes with it.
- **Controller down.** The host answers but the printer controller doesn't, for example Klipper shut down or OctoPrint with its serial port closed.

The last job's outcome (finished, cancelled or failed) is an extra fact on Ready, not a state of its own. Two reasons. OctoPrint reports these only as one-time events. And Bambu and Klipper keep saying FINISH, FAILED or "error" after a print even though the printer is ready to go again. My inference, not confirmed: Prusa's FINISHED behaves the same way.

## 4. Proposed mapping (proposal)

| Connection | Ready | Busy | Printing | Paused | Needs attention | Controller down | Lost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bambu | IDLE, FINISH, FAILED with no serious HMS | PREPARE, SLICING | RUNNING | PAUSE | serious or fatal HMS, or `print_error` while paused | n/a | no push for 30 s |
| Moonraker | webhooks ready + `print_stats` standby, complete, cancelled or error | standby while `idle_timeout` is Printing; webhooks startup | printing | paused | ? (a print that errors drops back to Ready with "failed") | `klippy_state` shutdown, error or disconnected | request fails |
| OctoPrint | ready | Starting, Finishing, Cancelling, Pausing | printing | paused | error | `closedOrError` / 409 | request fails |
| PrusaLink | IDLE, READY, FINISHED, STOPPED | BUSY | PRINTING | PAUSED | ERROR, ATTENTION | n/a | request fails |
| Duet | idle | busy and the other transitional values | processing / printing | paused | ? | halted, off, disconnected | request fails |
| Flashforge | ready, completed, cancel | busy, heating, calibrate_doing, downloading | printing | pause | error | n/a | request fails |
| Every other host | Unknown | | | | | | Not checked |

## 5. What it would take, cheapest first (proposal)

1. **Make "Unknown" the starting state and add "Not checked".** No card claims an activity or a connection it didn't read. This covers every connection type at once, and it only touches JusPrin-owned files.
2. **Read Moonraker activity in the poll that already runs every 10 s.** Add one call, `printer/objects/query?webhooks&print_stats&idle_timeout&virtual_sdcard`. That covers Klipper, and should also cover Qidi and Snapmaker U1 if they use the same API (not confirmed). Only JusPrin-owned files change. The other route is switching on upstream's disabled stream, but that edits an upstream file and also turns on upstream's Device-tab behavior, which upstream switched off on purpose.
3. **Read Bambu's Paused, Busy and Needs-attention states** from fields upstream already parses. Only JusPrin-owned files change.
4. **OctoPrint and PrusaLink** would each need a new poll. Later.

Still open:
- I haven't checked whether upstream's Moonraker agent also adds a second, always-Offline device card on Home.
- Whether Prusa's FINISHED is ready for the next job.
- Duet's progress fields.

I went through every way the app connects to a printer: Bambu, the 16 print-host types, upstream's newer printer agents, and JusPrin's own Moonraker polling. For each one I compared what the app reads today with what the printer's own API can report. The full tables are in the file I sent, `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/cf7649d3-46dd-4047-a831-32851ae18292/scratchpad/report/printer-states-by-connection.md`.

**What the app reads today (verified in code).** Only Bambu printers give the app a live print state, and even Bambu is shown imprecisely. A paused printer reads "Printing", and a failed print reads "Idle".
- **Moonraker:** JusPrin polls every 10 seconds, but only to check that the host answers and what filament is loaded.
- **Upstream's Moonraker agent:** it has code to read Klipper's print state, but upstream switched it off with `#if 0` and the comment "disable websocket for now" (`src/slic3r/Utils/MoonrakerPrinterAgent.cpp:2084`).
- **Every other host type** (OctoPrint, PrusaLink, Duet, Flashforge and the rest): the app reads no state at all. Their cards say "Idle" and a green "Connected · address" just because an address is saved.

**What the printers can report (from their docs).** Most APIs report the same handful of things: ready, busy with something like heating or homing, printing, paused, and an error. Moonraker, OctoPrint and Duet also report a case the others can't: the web host answers but the printer's controller is down. Your Pi this morning was exactly that. Finished and cancelled can't be treated as states. OctoPrint only sends them as one-time events, and Bambu and Klipper keep saying "finished" or "failed" long after the printer is ready again.

**Proposed model (a proposal; you haven't agreed to it).** The card should answer two separate questions.
- **Can the app reach the printer?** Not connected, Checking, Live, Lost, or Not checked. Not checked covers host types the app never polls.
- **What is the printer doing?** Unknown (the starting value), Ready, Busy, Printing, Paused, Needs attention, or Controller down. This is filled in only while the connection is Live and the type reports it.
- **The last job's outcome** (finished, cancelled or failed) would be an extra line on a Ready card, not a state.

The file maps each printer's raw values onto these states.

**Decision needed: should the card use these two questions and these states?** It's your call because it changes what every card says for every printer brand. One alternative is to keep a single state field and only add Unknown. That's less work, but "Klipper is shut down" and "the Pi doesn't answer" would still look the same. My pick is the two-question model as listed.

**Decision needed: which printers should show live activity first?** You decide where the effort goes. These are the steps, cheapest first:
1. Make Unknown the starting state and add Not checked. No card would claim anything it didn't read. That's a small change, in JusPrin-owned files only.
2. Read Klipper's state in the poll that already runs every 10 seconds. That's one extra Moonraker call, also in JusPrin-owned files only.
3. Split Bambu's Paused, Busy and Needs-attention out of the fields upstream already parses.
4. Add new polls for OctoPrint and PrusaLink.

My pick is steps 1 and 2 now, then step 3, with step 4 later.

Two things are still open. I haven't checked whether upstream's Moonraker agent also puts a second, always-Offline card on Home. Duet's progress fields are unconfirmed.

- [Why the Moonraker skill didn't guide the chat well](#local_262aaa6e-aa9c-48de-868d-d4285742aa4c) wrote a draft guide for writing connection skills at `agent-docs/jusprin/connection-skill-guide.md`. It switches the main window to Orca's Device page, which always shows the project's selected printer. It hasn't edited anything and is waiting for your choice of fix; open that session to see the options.

<!-- reply 3 -->
> Can the app reach the printer? Not connected, Checking, Live, Lost, or Not checked. Not checked covers host types the app never polls.

I'm not sure if I'm convinced. The users really don't care too much about if the connection is lost or not checked. To them it's just not connected. And if that's the case, they need to have a way to decide if it's expected. For example, the printer, they know the printer is powered down, or if it's not expected, how to troubleshoot it.

<!-- reply -->
> What is the printer doing? Unknown (the starting value), Ready, Busy, Printing, Paused, Needs attention, or Controller down. This is filled in only while the connection is Live and the type reports it.

I think you are over engineering it. Users already have too many things to be confused about. Now we want to confuse them more with two slightly different status. To them, the most intuitive way is that if the printer is not connected, then there's no such thing as a status except it's not connected. Otherwise, they probably have the status if the printer is connected. They want to quickly know that if it's printing, which in is the same as busy, right? Why do they it if we make busy and printing different status, it only confuse them, right? And what do you mean by controller down?

<!-- reply -->
> The last job’s outcome (finished, cancelled or failed) would be an extra line on a Ready card, not a state.

We can simply hide this when this is unknown


I think you are over engineering it. Let's do just one status. A status that user can intuitively understand without going through all these help documents to understand the subtle difference between all all of them. 

Come up with a list that users can intuitively understand and can be reasonably mapped to  the different status of those different connection types. Then come up with a table for how you plan to map them.

Your two side sessions have new results. The Moonraker skill session listed every failed connection attempt from Oct 31 to Nov 4, each on its own, with no patterns drawn yet. The monitor-button session is still working.

You're right that the two-question version was too much. Here is a single status list. This is still a proposal.

## The statuses

- **Not connected.** The app can't reach the printer, or the printer can't print because its controller isn't running. The card says why, and when it was last connected ("Last connected 3 hours ago"), so the person can tell whether that's expected because they switched it off. Reconnect opens the troubleshooting chat when the check fails.
- **Ready.** It's connected and not printing. When the printer reports how the last print ended, a short line says "Last print finished", "cancelled" or "failed". Otherwise there's no line.
- **Printing.** This includes heating, homing and leveling for a job. Progress and the job name show when the printer reports them.
- **Paused.** I kept this one apart from Printing. A paused print usually means the person has to do something, like reloading filament after a runout. On a card that says "Printing" they would never notice.
- **Needs attention.** It's connected, but it reports an error the person must clear. The printer's own message is shown.
- **Connected.** The app can reach the printer, but this connection type doesn't tell it what the printer is doing. No activity word is shown.
- **Connecting…** This appears only in the first few seconds after the app starts or a printer is added, before the first answer comes in. Without it, a working printer would read "Not connected" for those seconds.

You asked what "controller down" meant. A Klipper printer has two parts. A small computer such as a Raspberry Pi runs the web interface. Klipper, a program on that computer, actually drives the printer's board. This morning your Pi answered, but Klipper said "Lost communication with MCU". The MCU is the printer's board, and that message usually means the printer is switched off. To the person, the printer simply isn't usable. So I've put that case under Not connected, with Klipper's message as the reason. It's no longer a status of its own.

## How each connection type maps

| Connection | Not connected | Ready | Printing | Paused | Needs attention | Connected |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bambu (LAN or cloud) | no data for 30 s | IDLE, FINISH, FAILED | RUNNING, PREPARE, SLICING | PAUSE | serious or fatal health (HMS) message | — |
| Klipper via Moonraker (also Qidi, Snapmaker U1; not confirmed) | no answer; Klipper not running or shut down, with its message | standby, complete, cancelled, error | printing | paused | — (a Klipper error stops Klipper, so it lands in Not connected) | — |
| OctoPrint | no answer; OctoPrint not connected to the printer (closedOrError, 409) | operational, ready | printing, starting, finishing, cancelling | paused, pausing | error | — |
| PrusaLink, Prusa Connect | no answer | IDLE, READY, FINISHED, STOPPED | PRINTING, BUSY | PAUSED | ERROR, ATTENTION | — |
| Duet | no answer; halted, off, disconnected | idle | processing, busy, starting, changingTool, resuming, cancelling | paused, pausing | — | — |
| Flashforge | no answer | ready, completed, cancel | printing, busy, heating, calibrate_doing, downloading, canceling | pause, pausing | error | — |
| Elegoo, Creality K series | connection drops | idle | printing, plus preparing codes | paused | error code | — |
| Repetier, MKS, ESP3D, FlashAir, AstroBox, Obico, SimplyPrint, 3DPrinterOS, CrealityPrint host | upstream's connection test fails | — | — | — | — | connection test passes |

The "last print" line comes from Bambu FINISH or FAILED, Klipper complete, cancelled or error, Prusa FINISHED or STOPPED, and Flashforge completed or cancel. Every other card hides it.

Today the app reads only the Bambu row, and only partly. Every other host card claims "Idle" and "Connected" without having read either.

**Decision needed: should I build this list now, and how far?** It's your call because it changes what every printer card says.
- **Smallest step:** Bambu reads all its statuses, Klipper reads its state in the poll that already runs every 10 seconds, and every other host shows only Connected or Not connected. It uses upstream's existing connection test, and only JusPrin-owned files change.
- **Cost of that step:** it adds a periodic connection test against hosts the app currently leaves alone, including cloud services like SimplyPrint. I haven't checked their rate limits.
- **Bigger step:** also reading OctoPrint's and Prusa's activity. That needs a new poll for each.

My pick is the smallest step now, and OctoPrint and Prusa later. Do you want me to go ahead with that?

It looks good, but let's do the design first. Create a board to show these states. Also, when you are building the board, you need to consider other fields and whether or not they can be shown as well as the card expanded/collpased.  do we actually need a collapsed status or we should just always make the card expand it? It just shrink or grow based on how many fields are available to show?

The two Claude artifacts are now the design source of truth: the Design System (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the "JusPrin v2" canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v). They started as copies of Figma ([[jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact]]), but they are no longer re-synced from it. **Why:** design changes now happen in the artifacts, so a Figma-based argument or a "change Figma" proposal points at a dead file. **How to apply:** check designs by reading the artifact files (Artifact read with `path`, e.g. `project/-.dc.html` on the canvas); never suggest editing Figma or waiting for Figma seat allowance; when citing a design, name the artifact board, not a Figma node. Describe what the board actually draws, not what a component's internal properties imply: a menu row with no fill or border draws no shape at all, so it is not "a square row". Older memories that say "Figma is the source of truth" ([[design-token-sync-decisions]], [[figma-jusprin-v2-file]]) are superseded on that point. **Restated by Kenneth later on 2026-10-20:** "from now on, we should assume claude design artifact is the up to date design. figma is out of date." Docs changed the same day (uncommitted on jusprin-newui): agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md no longer points at Figma, and the repo skill .claude/skills/figma-agent-design is marked retired. **Also frozen (Kenneth, 2026-10-27):** the old Claude Design project "OrcaSlicer AI redesign concepts" (claude.ai/design/p/d981c5e2-…, files like `Orca Chat Panel.dc.html`). It is history for how a decision was reached, never the current design. For the chat panel, including G-code entries and print bands, the current boards are the five `main-print-timeline-panel-full*` boards on the canvas's Main Page. **The canvas moved (2026-10-27):** VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v is itself frozen ("JusPrin v2 (frozen 2026-10-27)" title, a `frozen-pointer-*` note on every page). The current canvas is https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ, with numbered board names (`main-05-print-timeline-panel-full-no-revert`, `main-07-…full`, `agent-ui-01-timeline-cards-manufacturing-history-state-matrix`) and shared parts as `` components that render.py can't draw. Check the canvas title before editing. On it (version 1793132250-e29e) `plates-26e3-project-print-history` and the state matrix were redrawn to the G-code design (matrix now 3 variants, 772 px tall). I also edited 26e3 on the frozen canvas by mistake (version 1793132033-a81d); at Kenneth's request it was restored byte-for-byte to the original BUILD 1 board in version 1793132895-0706. **How to apply:** when a memory note, commit message, doc or old plan cites a Figma frame, node id or value, treat it as history and check the artifact board instead. Edit the artifacts directly (recipe in [[jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact]]); never re-sync them from Figma, which would overwrite newer design. === jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact Two private artifacts in Kenneth's Claude account mirror the Figma file ([[figma-jusprin-v2-file]]). Since 2026-10-20 these artifacts ARE the source of truth ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]); edit them directly. The Figma re-sync steps below are history. 1. Design System: https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL (version 9) - `tokens.json` + `tokens.css`, 37 coded React components (`window.JusPrin`). - Each component card: every variant Figma draws, a Light and a Dark panel, then the coded component. The page lists them as one flat table in bundle order with code names; it draws no group headings. - `screens//.spec.txt` (166) + `screens/index.json`: plain files for agents, one resolved line per layer. 2. Design canvas "JusPrin v2": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v (version 7): 10 pages with Figma's names in Figma's order, 198 artboards at their Figma x,y and in Figma's layer order, each drawn in the Light or Dark mode Figma sets on it; "… · Light & Dark" review frames are drawn whole. Tools, reads and backups are durable now, outside the repo: `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/` — start with its `README.md` (step-by-step re-sync). `published/` is an exact copy of what is live; `backup-2026-10-13-before-reimport/` holds the earlier state with the scripts that reproduce it byte for byte. How Kenneth wants a re-sync done (2026-10-13): back up first, re-import, then compare the backup with the new import so nothing already in sync regresses. The method that worked, in order: - rebuild from the old reads and require byte-identical output (proves the scripts); - re-read Figma with the old script and diff the reads (proves Figma unchanged: all 14 files were identical); - only then change scripts, and explain every file `compare_builds.py` reports; - score every artboard against Figma's own page screenshots (`visual_compare.py`) and allow no artboard to score worse. Result of that run: 0 artboards further from Figma, 36 closer; boards within 5 of Figma (0–255 scale) went from 99 to 122 of 186; all 37 cards and 163 of 166 spec files came out byte-identical; tokens matched Figma's variables exactly. What the screenshot comparison caught that file checks could not: dark panels I had added behind dark variants (Figma has none), frames forced dark by a "dark" in their name (use Figma's `explicitVariableModes` instead), a frame half light and half dark through a nested mode, sets whose background is a two-stop linear gradient, Figma's GRID layout (children need their own positions), and small frames centred in the 40px-minimum artboard instead of top-left. Other traps: an absolutely positioned layer followed by in-flow siblings paints over them in HTML (give the later siblings `position:relative`); Figma tints icons with a mask plus a coloured rectangle; the Artifact tool's bulk read prints small text files into context, so have a background agent do large backups; a session scratchpad is wiped on restart — never keep the only copy of tools there; when two reads of a page exist, keep the later one by timestamp. Known gaps: photographs and 3D renders are flat placeholders (the 16 worst scores are all such screens); radial and image fills are placeholders; Figma stacks 12 dark screens on top of light ones on "Printer & Material Settings" and the canvas keeps that; ProjectCard and PrinterCard variants are stacked in Figma and laid out in a row on the canvas; "Add Printer Flow (Obsolete)" is not read; Notice/Strip drifts a few px vertically. Figma vs code differences Kenneth has not ruled on (the artifacts hold Figma's): dark status colours (Figma #4CAF82 / #E07080 / #E8B84A, code #58B894 / #F07A8E / #E9B960), `radius/full` 10 vs `pill` 9999, Button/Icon 32px vs 26px, Menu/Row 36px full-width hover vs the app's 32px inset rows ([[header-menu-values-kenneth-kept]]). See also [[figma-mcp-view-seat-limit]] and [[claude-in-chrome-lives-in-claude-profile]]. Direct editing (2026-10-20): work on a copy of the live files (`figma-mirror/live-` -> `work/`), publish only the changed files, then rsync `work/` into `published/`. The canvas holds its own copy of the design system in `project/ds/jusprin/` (tokens.css/json, components/bundle.*) — change both artifacts together. `tools/composer/render.py` screenshots boards with headless Chrome (no type runtime needed); measure natural board heights in the built-in browser and fix both the board file and canvas.json (`resize_board.py`). `index.d.ts` must be published with contentType text/plain. The DS card height lives in the `@dsCard height=` comment. Added then: `surface-raised-hover` (menu-row highlight, dark #3B3047) and `component-composer-maxLines` (8); the new Composer is drawn by `tools/composer/composer_html.py`. Publishing (2026-10-20, filament step): a publish is refused as "haven't viewed the latest version" unless this session did a plain `read` of the artifact url (path reads alone do not count). Headless Chrome hangs when another Chrome holds the default profile: pass `--user-data-dir=` (render.py now does). MenuRow has `detail`, `detailTone: 'warning'` and `meta` since then. **Trap found 2026-10-20 (turn line work):** `figma-mirror/tools/bundle.src.js`, `bundle.src.css` and `index.src.d.ts` were STALE against the live Design System bundle (menu-row detail/meta and the Composer menus had been added directly in the artifact). Running build_components.py or assembling from those sources regresses the live bundle. Patch the live files (published/… copies, verified equal to the artifact by sha) and refresh the tools sources from the patched result; `tools/composer/add_turn_line_boards.py` and the ChatTurnActivity card were done that way. The DS page generates `tokens.css` itself: never publish it to the DS, only to the canvas's `project/ds/jusprin/` copy. Adding a coded component = patch bundle.js (function + header list + __EXPORTS__), bundle.css, index.d.ts (props + window typing), tokens.json, a hand-written `components//preview.html` card with `@dsCard height=` measured by rendering it with React from unpkg, README.md's component list, and `design-system.json` lastChange in the last call. **2026-10-26 (setup card rework):** `tools/composer/setup_card_lib.py` draws the two-part card as board markup, spec lines and the coded component from one props dict; `build_setup_card_rework.py` runs the whole rework (cards, screens, calibration, sticky, new, canvas, ds) into `work-setup-card/`. The mirror's `published/canvas` had drifted by three onboarding-v1 boards (fetched back); the live canvas.json, not the mirror's, is the base for an index publish. Version ids before and after each publish are logged in the README ("Versions before the setup-card rework"): the tool cannot list versions, so write them down at publish time. Both artifacts' versions bump when their Artifact type re-releases, so a new version id alone does not mean content changed. `tools/bundle.src.*` and `index.src.d.ts` were refreshed from the published bundle; `heights.json` in the work dir holds every measured board height. === canvas-boards-from-bundle-rules Kenneth, 2026-10-21, on the calibration page I drew: "It looks like you didn't follow this hygiene. read design guidelines in readme, and fix your own sloppiness", then "I suspect there were more sloppiness in the boards you designed". He was right on both counts. I had copied markup from older canvas boards (the printer-menu board at 13 px rows, the stale ds-chat-reply-choice board) and from memory (a Home kebab with no Connect…, a black Remove, a 220 px width, the filament menu in an old order), instead of from the two sources that are authoritative. **Why:** rule 5 of "Writing UI code" (agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md) says the design system wins, and the design system's truth is its coded bundle (`figma-mirror/published/ds/project/components/bundle.css`, classes `.jp-*`), not any one board on the canvas: boards drift (the printer-menu board draws rows at 13 px, the reply choice board draws the pre-capsule style). For surfaces the bundle has no component for (the printer receipt, a sent photo in a message), the app's own CSS and TSX are the source. **How to apply:** before drawing a board, dump the bundle rules for every component used (`grep '\.jp-' bundle.css`) and read the app's row set for every menu (Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp, Shell/FilamentMenu.cpp, HomeUI PrinterMenu.tsx) and the app's CSS for chat pieces (AgentUI/styles.css). Also wrong the first time: the chat header named the project where the app names the chat (3 to 7 words, kConversationTitleInstructions); the pinned card was the stale "CURRENT SETUP · See all" board, not the app's Setup summary (`.current-setup*`: label + state header in Metadata Bold, purpose as Body Bold title, presets line, plan headline, Label Bold metrics with 14 px glyphs, hairline, All settings link; out of date drops the accent and uses the attention block); the composer placeholder was not the approved board's. Draw rows at Body 14 / 36 px (`.jp-menu-row`), popovers on surface-raised 280 wide, reply choices as capsules on surface-subtle, user bubbles 10/12 padding radius-medium at 75% width, tool cards on surface-subtle, project cards 293 wide with one status line, and no annotation tags ("NEW") inside a drawn component. State in the caption which rows are new. Known DS-vs-canvas inconsistency not mine to settle: `.jp-bubble-agent` has an avatar; the app and the timeline boards draw agent prose without one. Related: [[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]], [[jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact]], [[calibration-design-decisions]]. Moved from the index 2026-11-01: the calibration page had eight such misses, all fixed. === show-design-in-the-screen On 2026-10-28 I published four boards for the "from the file" printer-chip mark: the header strip alone, the chip's states, the menu popover, the header after a choice. Kenneth: "So you drew the mark out of the thin air in the vacuum? Where should they be attached to? … do you know how to show a design to a human being?" He was looking at the Printer & Material Settings page, where every board is a whole 1280×800 Prepare screen. **Why:** a reviewer judges a change by what surrounds it: the bed it sits over, the pane beside it, the message that follows. A strip with no screen gives nothing to attach the change to. **How to apply:** every review board is the whole screen at the app's size (1280×800 for Prepare), composed the way the canvas's existing screens are: header, viewport, Agent pane with the shared components (`comp-chat-header`, `comp-pinned-setup-card`, `comp-composer` via ``), and the timeline rows the app really showed. Use the walkthrough's real screenshots for the viewport (crop, upload as a canvas asset, ``), and the app's real strings. A component-states board may come last, as a detail, never first or alone. Builder pattern: `figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_file_printer_page.py` (second version). Related: [[canvas-boards-from-bundle-rules]], [[file-printer-switch-decisions]]. === render-canvas-boards-with-render-dc `python3 figma-mirror/tools/composer/render_dc.py [--dark] ...` serves `/project`, maps `support.js` to `/runtime/dc-runtime.js` (the artifact's `artifact-type/dc-runtime.js`) and `/_blob/` through `/runtime/blobs.json`, and shoots headless Chrome at 2x with its own `--user-data-dir`. 21 boards take about 22 s. `--dark` flips the board's theme prop. A working `work-credits/` exists from the 2026-11-01 credits page. Also learned drawing that page: anything absolutely placed over the Prepare screen needs a z-index above the composer band's, or the band paints over it. `figma-mirror/published/canvas` is stale (old board names), so pull live files with Artifact read `paths` + `out_dir` rather than copying from it. Related: [[canvas-boards-from-bundle-rules]], [[jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact]]. === artifact-watch-crosstalk On 2026-10-21 Kenneth found another session's canvas comments (a "Calibration · Printer & Filament" page) being auto-replied to and reported in this session, and asked how to make this session ignore it. Cause: every publish to a Claude artifact arms a watch with comment auto-replies in the publishing session. Two sessions working on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v) or the Design System (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) both get every comment sent to Claude, wherever it is on the artifact. **Why:** the wrong session answers a thread about work it doesn't know, and its reply can contradict the session that owns the boards. **How to apply:** after a publish, stop the watch (ArtifactComments action "watch", on: false) unless Kenneth said this session owns the artifact's comments. Re-read the live artifact before publishing again, since another session may have published since. Related: [[jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact]], [[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]. === mockup-strings-from-real-output When sketching UI that summarises OrcaSlicer data (the setup summary card, 2026-10-07/08), do not hand-type ideal strings such as "Brim 8 mm outer" or a shortened preset name. Kenneth challenged exactly those: there was no rule that produces them, and measuring showed they did not fit the line either. **Why:** Kenneth said an earlier agent drew a good-looking mockup, then at implementation found no way from raw data to the "smart" summary and fell back to hard-coding a few fields (the 13-key `kSetupKeys` list). He wants that trap avoided, not repeated. **How to apply:** Before proposing a layout, write the generic rule, run it over real data (all settings, all shipped preset names), measure lengths against the real line width, and fill the sketch only from that output. Say plainly which phrasing only a model could write. He asked for a 5% random sample of the output to review, not the full table. The formatter is `Workspace/SettingDisplay.hpp`, tested by `setting_display_tests` (links libslic3r only, builds in minutes in a fresh worktree). See [[figma-dump-then-measure-parity]]. **2026-10-08 follow-up (finishing the Codex implementation, worktree `~/.codex/worktrees/setup-card-differences/JusPrin`, branch `codex/setup-card-differences`, uncommitted):** Kenneth said the other agent matched the design terribly. Its fixtures did match; what was wrong only showed in the real app and in what it deleted. Checks that found the defects, in the order worth repeating: - Restore the tests an agent deleted for behaviour the handoff said stays unchanged, then run them: this caught a saved card showing "Agent is applying…". - Pixel-diff, not eyeball: render the built fixtures into the mockup's own frame (same scaffold CSS, 320 px, light and dark), screenshot both with headless Chrome, `PIL.ImageChops.difference(...).getbbox()`. - Real app: `JusPrinShellHarness --light-ui|--dark-ui --setup-differences-capture ` edits process, filament, printer and object settings and photographs the web view. Use `capture_web_view` (WebKit snapshot); `write_screen_capture` gives blank 810-byte PNGs from a shell. - `Search::OptionsSearcher::get_option` only knows settings visible in the current user mode and returns a neighbour otherwise; `get_group_and_category(";")` (try `key#0` for per-extruder keys) is mode-independent. - `PREVIEW_OUT=... npx vitest run` with no filter lets every `*.preview.test.tsx` overwrite the same file; name the test. - Kenneth, same day: hard-coded setting names are "a big problem" wherever they are, not only on the card. The chat timeline's agent pill (`ChangeRows.tsx`) looked up "Wall loops" and infill by label; he wanted it shown with a screenshot and gone. Do not leave such code with a note; fix it and show before/after. - A live capture only proves the design if the app is in the mockup's state. Mine first showed a project with no recorded purpose, so the title and lines differed and he called it out. The harness mode now records a purpose and applies a patch through `host.tools().propose("intent_update" / "settings_apply_patch", …, )`, slices, and waits out the 60 s "Updated" window. - Landed 2026-10-08: cherry-picked onto `jusprin-newui` in the main checkout as 198c64606f (not pushed by me), after Kenneth rewrote the approval-removal history (eb45279cd5). `origin/temp/setup-card-differences` (4650dd3093) is the pre-rewrite copy. === show-the-board-when-asking-kenneth On questions about "6a", "6b" and "7c": "I have no idea what you are talking about and how I can find 6a and 6b." and "Again, show me how I can find what you are talking about." **Why:** board numbers are my builder's labels, and the canvas holds dozens of boards across pages, so he can't answer about something he can't find. A session brief using those numbers doesn't make them his. **How to apply:** in anything Kenneth reads, name the screen by what a person sees, give the canvas page and heading it sits under, and send the PNG with SendUserFile, cropped when the point is small. Say what to look at in the picture. Related: [[ask-decisions-in-full]], [[write-like-a-person]], [[show-design-in-the-screen]]. === credits-boards-live-on-flow-pages Decided after Kenneth's review, relayed by the pricing session: canvas version 69. 1a to 1d, 6a, 6b on "On boarding experience"; 2a to 2c, 3a to 3d, 7a to 7c on "Compositions" beside the Composer; 4a to 4c on "Agent setup & Preferences"; 8a to 8d on "Print history"; 0 (five rules), 5a, 5b, 9 on "Credits & plans". **How to apply:** new credits boards go on their flow's page through the `LAYOUT` table in `figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_credits_page.py`, with "Credits" in the canvas name so a search finds the set. Related: [[print-report-lives-on-history-entry]].
