"""Screenshot canvas boards with the canvas's own Design Component runtime, so <dc-import> boards render whole
(render.py draws them blank). Serves <project dir> on a local port with ./support.js = the runtime saved from the
artifact's artifact-type/dc-runtime.js and /_blob/<id> mapped by blobs.json, then runs headless Chrome with its own
--user-data-dir. Usage: render_dc.py <work dir holding project/ and runtime/> <out dir> [--dark] <board.dc.html>..."""
import functools, http.server, json, re, socketserver, subprocess, sys, tempfile, threading
from pathlib import Path
args = sys.argv[1:]
dark = '--dark' in args
if dark: args.remove('--dark')
work, out, names = Path(args[0]), Path(args[1]), args[2:]
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
proj, runtime = work / 'project', work / 'runtime'
blobs = json.loads((runtime / 'blobs.json').read_text()) if (runtime / 'blobs.json').exists() else {}
chrome = '/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome'
class H(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def translate_path(self, path):
        p = path.split('?')[0]
        if p.endswith('/support.js'): return str(runtime / 'dc-runtime.js')
        if p.startswith('/_blob/'):
            b = blobs.get(p[7:])
            if b: return str(runtime / b)
        return super().translate_path(path)
    def do_GET(self):
        # --dark: the board's theme prop defaults to dark, the way the canvas's Theme switch sets it.
        if dark and self.path.split('?')[0].endswith('.dc.html') and 'board=1' in self.path:
            s = Path(self.translate_path(self.path)).read_text()
            s = s.replace('"theme":{"editor":"enum","options":["light","dark"],"default":"light"}', '"theme":{"editor":"enum","options":["light","dark"],"default":"dark"}')
            b = s.encode(); self.send_response(200); self.send_header('Content-Type', 'text/html; charset=utf-8'); self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(b))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(b); return
        return super().do_GET()
srv = socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), functools.partial(H, directory=str(proj)))
srv.daemon_threads = True
threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
port = srv.server_address[1]
for name in names:
    s = (proj / name).read_text()
    m = re.search(r'"\$preview":\{"width":(\d+),"height":(\d+)\}', s)
    w, h = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))
    png = out / (name.replace('.dc.html', '') + ('-dark' if dark else '') + '.png')
    subprocess.run([chrome, '--headless=new', '--disable-gpu', '--no-first-run', f'--user-data-dir={tempfile.mkdtemp()}', '--hide-scrollbars', f'--window-size={w},{h}', '--force-device-scale-factor=2',
                    '--virtual-time-budget=6000', f'--screenshot={png}', f'http://127.0.0.1:{port}/{name}?board=1'], check=True, capture_output=True, timeout=90)

content.text:
I added five boards to the JusPrin v2 canvas: [open the canvas](https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). They're on the Main Page, in a new row below the existing Home screens, under the title "Printer card · one status (proposal, 2026-11-04)". I sent you four of them as pictures.

**What the boards show:**
- **Every status as a card.** One card per status: Printing (one Bambu, one Klipper), Paused, Needs attention, Ready (one Bambu, one Klipper), Connected, Connecting…, and four kinds of Not connected (Klipper stopped, host silent, Bambu silent, never set up). Under each card, a caption says where its lines come from, or why a line is missing.
- **Home with three printers:** printing, ready, connected.
- **Home with the printers that need you:** your real case (Klipper stopped with "Lost communication with MCU 'mcu'" and "Last connected 3h ago"), a heatbed error, and a paused print with "AMS A Slot 1 filament has run out."
- **The same five printers twice.** Once with every card full, once with a one-line row for printers that need nothing.

**How the card's fields work** (all proposals):
- The status sits on one line under the name: a dot, the status word, and details. For example "Printing · 43% · 2h 14m left", then the job name and a progress bar. Only the dot carries color, so all the text stays readable.
- A line the printer doesn't report is left out, not filled in. Klipper gives no time left, so none is shown. Printers with no multi-filament unit get no spool row. "Last print failed" appears only when the printer says so.
- The card keeps the facts line (connection, address, model, nozzle), the print history link, and one action. That action is Launch monitor, Open printer window, Reconnect or Connect…, depending on the printer and its status.
- I left the camera preview off. The current canvas card has one, but the app doesn't, and the monitor already shows the camera. Without it the card is about 150 px shorter.

**On your question about collapsing.** Always-full cards are simpler: there's one shape, and nothing to click to find out what a printer is doing. The cost shows on the boards. A full card is 160–320 px tall, and the printer column has about 610 px. Even three printers make it scroll, and with five you see only two and a half. In the one-line version, a printer that needs nothing (Ready or Connected) takes one 42 px line with its name, status and spools. Printing, paused, needs-attention and not-connected printers get the full card. All five fit on screen.

**Decision needed: should every printer show its full card, or should printers that need nothing shrink to one line?** You decide what Home looks like for people with several printers.
- **Always full:** simplest, but the column scrolls from about three printers on.
- **One line when Ready or Connected:** everything fits and the printers that need you stand out. The cost is two shapes, plus a rule for when a card grows: it would grow on its own when the status changes, with no click.

My pick is the one-line version. I'd also sort printers that need you to the top, which the comparison board already does.

The real access code gave `ConnectStatusFailed` msg `-1` twice, about 24 s after `set_selected_machine`, the same as a made-up code. A one-off MQTT login to port 8883 (user `bblp`, 60 s timeout) answered CONNACK 0 with the real code and CONNACK 5 with a made-up one, so the code was right and the printer does tell them apart. During those failures TCP 8883 timed out for over a minute. An idle ping showed 64% loss and 15-50 s round trips, while the router answered in 3 ms and other Wi-Fi devices on the network were also slow.

Later on 2026-11-02, a saved LAN record at an address with no device at all (TCP 8883: "Host is down") also got `-1`, 12 s after selecting it, and the app's note said "refused". So -1 means at least "no connection made"; it does not need a printer to answer.

Correction, 2026-11-02 12:12: I blamed Kenneth's slow Wi-Fi, and a weak signal now looks unlikely. With no app running, about 3 hours after the last connection attempt from my tests, the printer lost 35% of pings at 9.6 s average while the router answered in 3 ms with no loss, and the printer reported -41 dBm and IDLE. A direct login with the right code was accepted but took 27.7 s, 26 s of it setting up TLS, which is longer than the ~24 s after which the plug-in reports -1. My hypothesis, unverified: on a slow printer the plug-in gives up before the code is tested. The cause of the slowness is unknown. **How to apply:** before concluding anything from a connect failure, check that the printer answers on TCP 8883 in under a second; `--printer-live-p1s <address> real-code` takes the code from `JUSPRIN_P1S_CODE`. === f8a1476539 Open each printer's monitor in its own window, and fix print-host printer windows
Before, the monitor button on a Bambu Lab printer's Home card jumped to
Orca's Device tab. That tab follows the project's selected printer, so with
a print-host printer selected it showed that printer's page instead, and
Home stayed on screen. Print-host printers had their own problems: one at an
address that never answers read "Connected", its window stayed white for
over a minute, and the header menu could not open it.

Bambu Lab monitor window:
- Home/MonitorWindow: Orca's MonitorPanel (the Device page) as a second
  instance in a window of its own, one per printer. It stays until the
  person closes it or quits the app. When Orca selects another machine, the
  window keeps its last picture, disables its controls and shows a warning
  row with a Close button; launching the monitor again opens a new window.
- Home/PopOutWindow: the frame both printer windows share, holding the safe
  way to destroy a web view (moved out of PrinterWindow unchanged).
- Shell/NoticeRow: the one-line sentence-and-button row, taken out of
  ClassicView's banner so the monitor window can use it too.
- The header printer menu's first row opens the same window as the Home
  card. SetupCommands::open_monitor() becomes monitored_device().

Print-host printers (OctoPrint, PrusaLink and others, not only Moonraker):
- Printers/HostLaneReader checks every named printer with a print host. A
  non-Moonraker host counts as answering when its web page returns any HTTP
  reply. Home's card now reads "Offline" for a host that never answers.
- Home/PrinterWindow shows "The printer's page didn't load", the address,
  and a Try again button when the page fails or has not loaded after 20
  seconds. PrinterWebView.cpp is unchanged.
- The header menu's first row reads Idle, Offline or "Checking connection…"
  for a print-host printer and opens its window.
- A second click on a printer whose address changed loads the new address
  in the open window; renaming a printer from Home keeps its window and
  retitles it.

The printer chat reads the same check, so it now reports an OctoPrint or
PrusaLink printer that answers as connected.

Tests: jusprin_tests pass (780 assertions in 138 test cases). The shell
harness --classic-switch (66 checks) and --printer-menu (65) pass. In
--printer-setup, every printer_window_* and host_lanes_* check passes. That
run was built with uncommitted printer-chat work from another session in the
same checkout, and its failing checks (nozzle_panel_*, panel_close_mid_test_*)
exercise that work's printer_host_connect tool and tool-call saves, not
these files. Each window problem was reproduced and then checked fixed in
the real app with a stand-in OctoPrint address and a local Klipper page; the

=== 8b4541dfc8 Add Docker print hosts, with cameras, for testing Moonraker and OctoPrint without a printer
tests/printer_hosts/docker-compose.yml starts the real host software with
simulated printer boards (was f51053cce2):

- 127.0.0.1:7130: Moonraker on Klipper, trusting every address (no key).
- 127.0.0.1:7131: a second Moonraker on the same Klipper that needs its API
  key (HTTP 401 without it).
- 127.0.0.1:5030: OctoPrint 1.11.2 with its bundled virtual printer, which
  needs its API key (HTTP 403 without it).

Klipper's board is Klipper's own AVR firmware running in simulavr, built on
prind's published tools image for the pinned Klipper tag so the firmware
always matches. Unpaced, simulavr fell behind on busy moves and Klipper shut
down with "Timer too close", so the board is built with -O2 and paced to half
of real time. printer.cfg matches the generic Klipper printer (MyKlipper 0.4
nozzle), works around simulavr's always-pressed endstops and fixed
thermistors, and defines PRINT_START/PRINT_END, so that printer's G-code
prints unchanged. keys.sh prints both keys as shell exports.

Cameras (was 5e23dc286b): a go2rtc container on port 7140 serves one camera
per printer, an ffmpeg test pattern labelled with its printer and a UTC
clock at 10 frames a second, running only while someone is watching. Both
Moonrakers list the Klipper camera at /server/webcams/list; OctoPrint shows
its camera on the Control tab, and its start script sets the addresses on
every start. The addresses use 127.0.0.1, so a browser on the same computer
can open them. One limit: OctoPrint's server cannot fetch its own snapshot
for timelapses, because inside its container 127.0.0.1 is not the host.

Verified on macOS (Docker Desktop, arm64):
- shell_integration_harness --print-host-check, 11 cases: open Moonraker
  verified with Klipper ready; no key or a wrong key refused with 401/403 and
  the key form opened; the right key verified; OctoPrint at the Moonraker
  address verified (Moonraker's OctoPrint API); Moonraker at the OctoPrint
  address failed with 404; a closed port failed.
- A 20 mm cube sliced by the app's command line with the generic Klipper
  profile printed to "complete" on Klipper in about 20 minutes (estimate 10)
  with no shutdowns, and started printing on OctoPrint.
- Stopping the simulavr container makes Moonraker report Klipper "shutdown",
  "Lost communication with MCU 'mcu'"; starting it and restarting klipper
  returns to ready.
- Both camera feeds play in a browser, OctoPrint's Control tab shows its
  camera, both hosts report the camera addresses from empty volumes, three
  viewers at once each get 10 frames a second, and stopping the camera
  container leaves the addresses unanswered.

The Klipper/Moonraker fake on jusprin-newui-fakeprinter
(tests/printer_sim/fake_moonraker.py) was never on this branch; the docs that
pointed there now point to tests/printer_hosts/README.md.

=== 83a8431df2 Printer chat: connect in one tool call, with the connection skill from add time and truthful connection messages
Three changes to how the printer chat connects a printer, all from the
live chats of 2026-11-04 with a Klipper printer (a Moonraker in Docker
needing an API key, and a Raspberry Pi with Klipper shut down), where the
model told the person something false at the moment it mattered.

Connect in one tool call (was be77a9e996). The connect tool is split in
two: printer_host_connect for Moonraker and OctoPrint, printer_bambu_connect
for Bambu Lab printers. Each call tests during the call (up to 30 seconds
for a print host) and returns the outcome as its result, instead of a later
note. When a print host asks for a key, or a Bambu Lab printer needs its
access code, the call stays open and shows the app's form in the chat;
Connect, "Help me find the key/code" and Cancel each end the call with what
happened, in the host's own words and saying which key the test sent.
ToolExecutionCoordinator gains the one rule it lacked: a tool may return
pending and be finished later (finish_pending), be retitled while it waits,
and have the app's dialogs that open meanwhile listed in its result. The
prompt suite's strict check flags only real leaks (exact tool names,
camelCase fields, raw JSON from a tool result); the profile/preset/catalog
word check is dropped, as grading it would add about 30% to a run's cost.
Each run prints its token use. The shell harness's --print-host-check drives
the connect tool against Moonraker and OctoPrint, answering the form with a
key, MISSING or CANCEL. Known: a failed attempt's tool card still shows
"Done".

The connection skill from the moment there is a saved printer (was
1b7230f33f). Before, a chat got the skill only after the model's first
connection tool call, so in a chat that added a printer and connected right
away the standing prompt's own connecting steps were read first and
outranked the skill: the model gave the exact connect offer after the person
had already asked, and told someone with no API key to "use that form".
PrinterConversation::connection_skill() now returns a skill whenever the
chat has a saved printer that is not the project's stock one: with
printer_add's result in an Add chat, and on the first request of a chat
about an existing printer, picked by vendor (Bambu Lab gets connect_bambu
with issue_report_open, any other printer connect_print_host). The
m_connect_tried flag is gone. connect-moonraker and connect-octoprint are
merged into one connect-print-host skill. It tells the two apart, says what
someone with no key can do (trusted_clients in moonraker.conf, the key page
at Moonraker's own port, fetch-apikey.sh), and labels each statement as seen
in a run, from a named document, or a guess. The standing prompt's
connecting steps (the offer after adding, the Bambu-or-print-host first
step, credential_requested, the 30-second wait) move into the skills; the
prompt keeps that the connection is optional, never to ask for a credential
in chat, and what to say when someone stops. The prompt suite's runner sends
the skill as the app now does; its Choices check ignores a source list after
the Choices line, and its menu-path condition fails only a specific path

content.text:
The camera is back on the boards, but only on my machine so far. The request came through another session rather than directly from you, so I haven't published it to the canvas without your go-ahead.

**Camera.** I drew it the way the canvas's original printing card does: a 135 px picture with a LIVE tag. It's on Printing and Paused cards, for the Bambu printers and for the Klipper printer. A Klipper printer gets one only when Moonraker lists a camera, and the app doesn't read that list yet; the card's caption says so. It makes the printing card 412 px tall instead of 265, which changes what fits in the printer column (744 px of room):

| Board | Without camera | With camera |
|---|---|---|
| Three printers, full cards | Two whole, the third short by 11 px | Two whole, only the third's name visible |
| Five printers, full cards | Two whole, a third partly | Two whole, the third just peeking in |
| Five printers, one line for those that need nothing | All five fit | Two whole cards and part of one line; two lines hidden |

So with the camera on, even the one-line version scrolls whenever something is printing.

**New commits on jusprin-newui.** The side sessions' work landed as three commits:
- **83a8431df2:** the printer chat connects in one tool call, gets the connection skill from the moment a printer is added, and gives truthful connection messages. Its test baseline is 379 of 390 runs, against 382 for the old code.
- **8b4541dfc8:** Docker print hosts with cameras, for testing Moonraker and OctoPrint without a printer.
- **f8a1476539:** each Bambu printer's monitor opens in its own window, and print-host printer windows are fixed. The app now checks every print host, so a host that never answers reads "Offline". The commit says the Bambu window was checked on your real P1S.

One thing in f8a1476539 repeats the bug we traced this morning. The header printer menu now says "Idle" for any print host that merely answers (`SetupCommands.cpp`: answering is turned into Idle). Before, it said nothing. A Klipper printer that is shut down or mid-print would read "Idle" there too.

**Side sessions.** All are idle except [Compare P1S LAN connect: JusPrin vs vanilla OrcaSlicer](#local_388d3bd1-94fb-47cb-a1ad-21a32000cdd3), which is still running. The skill session reports that Orca's "Enable SSL(MQTT)" preference was off in your JusPrin settings, while a P1S accepts only encrypted connections. With your approval, a session turned it on at 13:41 and kept a backup. That may explain the code -1 failures, but I haven't checked it myself.
Publish

They're on the Main Page, under "Printer card · one status (proposal, 2026-11-04)". Before publishing, I checked that nobody had edited the five boards since my last publish. - **Three printers as full cards:** the first two cards are whole, and only the name of the third shows.

Yes, one decision is still open. It's written out in full below.

**Has anyone mapped the proposed statuses onto the real code?** No. I searched the transcripts of all the side sessions: none of them worked on the status list, and the only other mention is a forked session reading my memory note about it. What exists is my own code survey from yesterday. For each connection type, it records what the app reads from the printer today. It found that only Bambu printers report a live print state, and every other type reports none. The mapping table I gave you came from each printer's API documentation, not from the code.

That survey is also partly out of date. Commit f8a1476539 (the monitor-window commit, now on jusprin-newui) changed two things:
- The app now checks every print host, not just Moonraker. OctoPrint, PrusaLink and the others count as answering if their web page replies, and the Home card reads "Offline" for one that never answers. Connected and Not connected can now come from real readings for every host.
- The header printer menu now says "Idle" for any print host that merely answers (`Shell/SetupCommands.cpp`, where answering is turned into Idle). That's the same mistake we traced this morning, in a new place.

Mapping the statuses onto the code would mean taking each status and each connection type and finding the line that would produce it, or recording that nothing produces it yet. I can do that next if you want, as code reading only, with no live-model calls. It would also tell us which rows of the table can be built now and which need new polling.

**Decision needed: should a printer that needs nothing (Ready or Connected) shrink to a one-line row, or should every printer always show its full card?** It's your call because it decides how Home looks for anyone with more than two printers.
- **Always full:** one card shape, nothing to open. The cost: the printer column fits only about two printers when one is printing, because the camera makes a printing card 412 px tall in a 744 px column.
- **One line when Ready or Connected:** with nothing printing, five printers fit. A card grows back to full on its own when its status changes. The cost: two shapes to build and keep in step, and it still scrolls while a printer with a camera is printing.

My pick is the one-line version, with printers that need you sorted to the top.

I think the best design is to determine if each of those fields need to show. And let the card naturally grow or shrink based on how many fields are being shown.

You previously came up with this mapping table. 

<pasted_content id="0c7b">
How each connection type maps
Connection	Not connected	Ready	Printing	Paused	Needs attention	Connected
Bambu (LAN or cloud)	no data for 30 s	IDLE, FINISH, FAILED	RUNNING, PREPARE, SLICING	PAUSE	serious or fatal health (HMS) message	—
Klipper via Moonraker (also Qidi, Snapmaker U1; not confirmed)	no answer; Klipper not running or shut down, with its message	standby, complete, cancelled, error	printing	paused	— (a Klipper error stops Klipper, so it lands in Not connected)	—
OctoPrint	no answer; OctoPrint not connected to the printer (closedOrError, 409)	operational, ready	printing, starting, finishing, cancelling	paused, pausing	error	—
PrusaLink, Prusa Connect	no answer	IDLE, READY, FINISHED, STOPPED	PRINTING, BUSY	PAUSED	ERROR, ATTENTION	—
Duet	no answer; halted, off, disconnected	idle	processing, busy, starting, changingTool, resuming, cancelling	paused, pausing	—	—
Flashforge	no answer	ready, completed, cancel	printing, busy, heating, calibrate_doing, downloading, canceling	pause, pausing	error	—
Elegoo, Creality K series	connection drops	idle	printing, plus preparing codes	paused	error code	—
Repetier, MKS, ESP3D, FlashAir, AstroBox, Obico, SimplyPrint, 3DPrinterOS, CrealityPrint host	upstream’s connection test fails	—	—	—	—	connection test passes

The “last print” line comes from Bambu FINISH or FAILED, Klipper complete, cancelled or error, Prusa FINISHED or STOPPED, and Flashforge completed or cancel. Every other card hides it.

Today the app reads only the Bambu row, and only partly. Every other host card claims “Idle” and “Connected” without having read either.

Decision needed: should I build this list now, and how far? It’s your call because it changes what every printer card says.

Smallest step: Bambu reads all its statuses, Klipper reads its state in the poll that already runs every 10 seconds, and every other host shows only Connected or Not connected. It uses upstream’s existing connection test, and only JusPrin-owned files change.
Cost of that step: it adds a periodic connection test against hosts the app currently leaves alone, including cloud services like SimplyPrint. I haven’t checked their rate limits.
Bigger step: also reading OctoPrint’s and Prusa’s activity. That needs a new poll for each.
</pasted_content id="0c7b">

Anything I could not confirm from a source is marked unverified.

## Bambu (MQTT on the LAN, plus FTPS)
- **Camera:** X1 and P2S serve `rtsps://IP:322/streaming/live/1` with user `bblp` and the LAN access code. On H2S and H2D the same stream is off until enabled on the touchscreen. P1 and A1 send JPEG frames over TLS on port 6000, after a binary login packet. [video.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/video.md) The MQTT report carries `ipcam.rtsp_url`; the value `"disable"` means LAN live view is off. [ha-bambulab models.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/greghesp/ha-bambulab/main/custom_components/bambu_lab/pybambu/models.py)
- **Job, progress, time left:** `subtask_name` / `gcode_file`, `mc_percent`, `mc_remaining_time`. [mqtt.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/mqtt.md) The docs give no unit for remaining time; minutes is commonly assumed but unverified.
- **Thumbnail:** not in MQTT. ha-bambulab downloads the job's `.3mf` from the printer and caches it for the cover image. [models.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/greghesp/ha-bambulab/main/custom_components/bambu_lab/pybambu/models.py) The plate PNG path inside the 3mf is unverified.
- **Model:** `info.get_version.module[]` has `name`, `hw_ver`, `sn`, `sw_ver`; there is no product-name field in those docs. [mqtt.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/mqtt.md) ha-bambulab uses `info.device_type`, but where that comes from is unverified.
- **Nozzle:** `nozzle_diameter`, a string such as `"0.4"`. [mqtt.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/mqtt.md)
- **Filament:** `ams.ams[].tray[].tray_type` and `tray_color` (RRGGBBAA), plus `vt_tray` for the external spool and `tray_now` for the active one. [mqtt.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/mqtt.md)
- **Errors:** `hms[]`, `print_error`, `mc_print_error_code` are codes only. ha-bambulab turns them into text with `get_HMS_error_text` and `get_print_error_text`, and treats `50348044` as a user cancel. [models.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/greghesp/ha-bambulab/main/custom_components/bambu_lab/pybambu/models.py) Where its lookup table comes from is unverified.
- **Last outcome:** `gcode_state` FINISH or FAILED; a cancel is told apart by that error code. The previous job's data is cleared only when the next job starts, so the name stays until then. [models.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/greghesp/ha-bambulab/main/custom_components/bambu_lab/pybambu/models.py)
- **Temperatures:** `nozzle_temper`, `nozzle_target_temper`, `bed_temper`, `bed_target_temper`. [mqtt.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/mqtt.md)

## Moonraker / Klipper
- **Camera:** `/server/webcams/list` returns `stream_url`, `snapshot_url` and `service`. A URL may be relative to the Moonraker host, and `snapshot_url` is empty when the camera has no snapshot. [webcams](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/webcams/)
- **Job:** `print_stats.filename`. **Progress:** `display_status.progress` (from M73, falling back to file position) or `virtual_sdcard.progress`. [Status Reference](https://www.klipper3d.org/Status_Reference.html)
- **Time left: computed.** Take `estimated_time` from the file's metadata, in seconds, and subtract `print_stats.print_duration`. [file_manager](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/file_manager/), [Status Reference](https://www.klipper3d.org/Status_Reference.html)
- **Thumbnail:** metadata `thumbnails[]` with `width`, `height`, `relative_path`. The path is relative to the G-code file's folder, and you fetch it through `/server/files/gcodes/...`. That fetch path is my inference; it is not documented as such. [file_manager](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/file_manager/)
- **Model:** none in the [Status Reference](https://www.klipper3d.org/Status_Reference.html). The printer reports nothing; the slicer's name is in metadata `slicer`.
- **Nozzle:** the live extruder object has no nozzle diameter. The file's metadata has `nozzle_diameter`. Reading the `[extruder] nozzle_diameter` config option through the `configfile` object is unverified.

- **Camera:** `/api/settings` gives `webcam.streamUrl` and `webcam.snapshotUrl`. [settings](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/settings.html) Since 1.9, webcams are provided by plugins, with the old behaviour moved into a bundled "Classic Webcam" plugin. [forum](https://community.octoprint.org/t/unable-to-change-the-webcam-address/52031) I found no documented `/api/webcams` endpoint.
- **Job, progress, time left:** `/api/job` gives `job.file.name`, `progress.completion` and `progress.printTimeLeft` (units unstated). [job](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/job.html)
- **Thumbnail:** core has none. The PrusaSlicer Thumbnails plugin adds a `thumbnail` field to the file metadata. [OctoDash issue](https://github.com/UnchartedBull/OctoDash/issues/566)

- **Filament:** not available.

## PrusaLink
All fields below come from the [PrusaLink OpenAPI spec](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prusa3d/Prusa-Link-Web/master/spec/openapi.yaml).
- **Camera:** `/api/v1/cameras` lists `camera_id`, `config.name` and flags such as `connected`. A snapshot endpoint is unverified, and I did not confirm that MK4/XL/MINI firmware serves this endpoint.
- **Job:** `/api/v1/job` `file.display_name`, with `progress` and `time_remaining` in seconds. `/api/v1/status` also has `job.progress` and `job.time_remaining`.
- **Thumbnail:** `file.refs.thumbnail` and `file.refs.icon`.
- **Model:** no model field. `file.meta.printer_model` is what the file was sliced for.
- **Nozzle:** `/api/v1/info` `nozzle_diameter`.
- **Filament:** `/api/v1/info` has an `mmu` boolean only; per-slot data is not in the spec. `file.meta.filament_type` describes the file.
- **Errors:** `printer.status_printer.message`. The ATTENTION state carries no text.
- **Last outcome:** the states FINISHED, STOPPED and ERROR, with `job.id`. There is no history endpoint.
- **Temperatures:** `temp_nozzle`, `target_nozzle`, `temp_bed`, `target_bed`.

## Prusa Connect
This is a cloud service, not a LAN API. Its only documented public API is the camera one, where a camera pushes JPEGs with `PUT /v1/snapshot` and sends `PUT /v1/camera-info`. [camera-service docs](https://camera-service.prusa3d.com/docs/), [help](https://help.prusa3d.com/article/prusa-connect-camera-api_569012) I found no documented public API for reading printer status or snapshots, so every card field is unverified.

# When each printer card field shows, by connection type

Written 2026-11-04. Every field has one rule for when it shows, and that rule is the same for every printer. The connection type only decides whether the value exists. Today Bambu fills most of the card. Moonraker fills only the connection and the loaded filament. Every other print host fills only the fields the app keeps itself, plus a bare "Connected".

Sources: the code at jusprin-newui f8a1476539, and each printer API's docs (links in section 3). The rules in section 1 are a proposal Kenneth has not agreed to. Section 2 says what exists today.

## 1. The rule for each field (proposal)

The fields are listed top to bottom, as on the boards.

| Field | Shows when | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Name | Always | |
| ⋯ menu | At least one of settings, rename or remove is allowed | Today an unnamed Bambu LAN printer gets none, so its card has no menu |
| Camera | Status is Printing or Paused, and the app has a stream for this printer | |
| Status word | Always, one of: Printing, Paused, Needs attention, Ready, Connected, Connecting…, Not connected | Comes from the status table already proposed |
| Status detail after the dot | Printing: percent, plus "· 2h 14m left" when time left is known. Paused: "at 27%". Otherwise nothing | |
| Job name | The printer reports a current job (Printing, Paused, or Needs attention during a job) | |
| Progress bar | Same as the job name, and the percent is known | |
| Printer's message | Needs attention: always. Paused: when the printer gives a reason. Not connected: always, giving the reason | When the printer sends only a code, show a sentence with the code. When the app never reached the printer, the reason is the app's own words ("octopi.local isn't answering.") |
| "Last connected …" | Not connected, and the app knows when it last heard from the printer | Hidden when unknown |
| Facts line (connection kind · address · model · nozzle) | Always; each part shows when known | Model and nozzle come from the printer profile for every type, because few printers report them. The address shows for print hosts only |
| Loaded filament | The printer reports what is loaded right now | Never a remembered value on a card that is not connected |
| History link | At least one print or send record exists | The last print's outcome ("last finished Sun") goes here, only when the printer reports it |
| Button | Never set up: "Connect…". Not connected: "Reconnect". Connecting…: none. Otherwise: "Launch monitor" for Bambu, "Open printer window" for a host with a web page | |

## 2. Where each value comes from, per connection type

Key:
- **today**: the card shows it now.
- **in app**: the app already receives it but does not send it to the card.
- **API**: the printer reports it, and the app needs new reading code.
- **calc**: the card has to compute it or look it up.
- **—**: not available.
- **?**: not confirmed.

| Field | Bambu | Moonraker | OctoPrint | PrusaLink | Duet | Flashforge | Elegoo | Creality K | Other hosts* |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Activity part of the status | today, partly (paused reads Printing, failed reads Idle) | API | API | API | API | API | API | API | — |
| Connection part of the status | today | today | today, since f8a1476539 (any HTTP reply) | same | same | same | same | same | same |
| Camera | in app (stream fields; upstream's native player) | API `/server/webcams/list` | API, but the URL is often `localhost` | ? | — | API | API | API | — |
| Job name | in app `subtask_name` | API | API | API | API | API | API | API | — |
| Percent | today | API | API | API | calc | API | API | API | — |
| Time left | today | calc (file estimate minus time printed) | API | API | API | API (freezes while paused) | calc | API | — |
| Printer's message | calc (the app's HMS lookup exists) | API, text | API, text | API, text (ATTENTION has none) | API, text | code only | code only | code only | — |
| Last connected | in app, in memory only | in app, in memory only | in app, in memory only | same | same | same | same | same | same |
| Facts line | in app (connection kind, profile). Nozzle: today | in app (the host type is saved but not sent to the page) | same | same | same | same | same | same | same |
| Loaded filament | today (AMS, external spool) | today (`lane_data` or Happy Hare only) | — | — | API, name only, no colour | API, AD5X only | — | API, CFS only | — |
| Last print outcome | in app `gcode_state` FINISH/FAILED | API history, kept after the job | — (per file only) | API, until the next job | API, kept after the job | ? | API | — (only inferred) | — |
| History | today, prints | today, sends only | today, sends only | same | same | same | same | same | same |

*Other hosts are Prusa Connect, Repetier, MKS, ESP3D, FlashAir, AstroBox, SimplyPrint, Obico and 3DPrinterOS. For SimplyPrint and Obico, "answers" means the company's website answered, not the printer.

"Last connected" is in memory only for every type, so after a restart the line is hidden until the printer is heard again. Saving the time to disk would fix that.

## 3. API sources

- Bambu: OpenBambuAPI [mqtt.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/mqtt.md) and [video.md](https://github.com/Doridian/OpenBambuAPI/blob/main/video.md); ha-bambulab [models.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/greghesp/ha-bambulab/main/custom_components/bambu_lab/pybambu/models.py).
  - The unit of `mc_remaining_time` is unverified (minutes is assumed).
  - On H2S and H2D, the LAN stream is off until it is switched on at the printer.
- Moonraker: [webcams](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/webcams/), [history](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/history/), [file_manager](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/file_manager/), Klipper [Status Reference](https://www.klipper3d.org/Status_Reference.html).
- OctoPrint: [job](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/job.html), [printer](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/printer.html), [settings](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/master/api/settings.html).
- PrusaLink: [OpenAPI spec](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prusa3d/Prusa-Link-Web/master/spec/openapi.yaml).
  - The camera endpoint on MK4, XL and MINI firmware is unverified.
  - Prusa Connect has no documented public status API.
- Duet: [object model](https://github.com/Duet3D/RepRapFirmware/wiki/Object-Model-Documentation).
- Flashforge: [community docs](https://github.com/Parallel-7/flashforge-api-docs/wiki/HTTP-REST-API).
- Elegoo: [SDCP V3](https://github.com/cbd-tech/SDCP-Smart-Device-Control-Protocol-V3.0.0).
- Creality: [ha_creality_ws](https://github.com/3dg1luk43/ha_creality_ws).

## 4. Problems found on the way (not reproduced, not fixed)

- The header menu calls a print host "Idle" when it only answered (`Shell/SetupCommands.cpp:289`). This is the same kind of bug as the Home card's false "Idle".
- Reconnect on an unnamed Bambu card returns "This printer no longer exists." (`Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:162-166`, `751-753`).
- A print host that is printing reads "Idle" on Home.

content.text:
I went through every field on the printer card the same way I did the status table. For each field I checked what the code reads today, and what each printer's API can report. The result is a proposal: each field gets one rule for when it shows, and that rule is the same for every printer. The connection type only decides whether the field has a value. The card grows when more rules are met, and shrinks when fewer are.

**The rules, top to bottom:**
- **Name and facts line:** always shown. The facts line is connection kind, address, model and nozzle. Model and nozzle come from the printer profile, because hardly any printer reports them itself.
- **Camera:** only while the printer is printing or paused, and only if the app has a stream for that printer.
- **Job name and progress bar:** only while the printer reports a job.
- **Time left:** added after the percent when the printer reports it.
- **Printer's message:**
  - Always shown on "Needs attention".
  - On "Paused", shown when the printer gives a reason.
  - On "Not connected", always shown, giving the reason.
  - If the printer sends only an error code, the card shows a sentence that includes the code.
- **"Last connected …":** only on "Not connected", and hidden when the app doesn't know.
- **Loaded filament:** only when the printer reports what is loaded right now. A card that isn't connected never shows a remembered value.
- **History link:** shown when at least one print or send record exists. The last print's result ("last finished Sun") goes in this line, only when the printer reports it.
- **Button:**
  - "Connect…" if the printer was never set up.
  - "Reconnect" when it's not connected.
  - No button while connecting.
  - Otherwise, "Launch monitor" for Bambu, or "Open printer window" for a print host.

**What fills those fields today:**
- **Bambu** fills most of the card. Its job name, message, camera and last print result are already in the app, but they aren't sent to the card.
- **Moonraker** fills only whether it answers and the loaded filament. Its job, progress, messages, camera and print history all need new code, but the API provides all of them.
- **Other print hosts** (OctoPrint, PrusaLink, Duet, Flashforge, Elegoo, Creality) get only the fields the app keeps itself, plus a bare "Connected". Each would need its own status reading.
- **"Last connected"** is kept only in memory for every printer. After a restart it stays hidden until the printer is heard from again.

**Decision needed:** which printers' readings get built first. One option is Moonraker first, then Bambu.
- Moonraker needs one extra query in the check that already runs every 10 seconds, plus one call for its camera list. Only JusPrin's own files change. It's also the type of printer you test with.
- Bambu's job, message and last result are already in the app, so they are cheap to pass to the card.
- The Bambu camera costs more. Upstream plays it with a native player, and getting it into the web-page card would need new work. That's my estimate; I haven't checked it.

The other option is Bambu first, which covers the most users sooner. OctoPrint and PrusaLink would come after either. My pick is Moonraker first, then Bambu's fields that are already in the app, then the Bambu camera. Which order do you want?

I also found three likely bugs. I haven't reproduced or fixed any of them:
- The header menu calls a print host "Idle" just because it answered (`SetupCommands.cpp:289`).
- Reconnect on a Bambu card without a saved name fails with "This printer no longer exists."
- A print host that is printing shows "Idle" on Home.

The full table, with links to each API's docs, is at `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/cf7649d3-46dd-4047-a831-32851ae18292/scratchpad/report/printer-card-fields-by-connection.md`.

Let's make it always on as long as the stream is available.

# Print hosts without a printer

Docker containers that run the real print-host software, for testing the app's
Moonraker and OctoPrint paths: connecting, API keys, status, cameras, and
sending a print. Only the printer boards and the cameras' pictures are
simulated. Bambu printers are covered by the in-process fake instead
([Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md)).

| Address | What answers | Key |
|---|---|---|
| `http://127.0.0.1:7130` | Moonraker on Klipper, trusts every address | none |
| `http://127.0.0.1:7131` | the same Klipper through a second Moonraker | needed; HTTP 401 without it |
| `http://127.0.0.1:5030` | OctoPrint 1.11.2 with its bundled virtual printer | needed; HTTP 403 without it |
| `http://127.0.0.1:7140` | the printers' cameras ([Cameras](#cameras)) | none |

Klipper's board is simulavr, an AVR simulator running Klipper's own firmware,
set up from [prind](https://github.com/mkuf/prind). OctoPrint's printer is its
[Virtual Printer](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/devel/bundledplugins/virtual_printer.html)
plugin, which acts like a Marlin printer on a serial port.

## Start and stop

Needs Docker (Docker Desktop on macOS and Windows).

```bash
docker compose -f tests/printer_hosts/docker-compose.yml up -d
```

The first start builds the simulavr image, which nobody publishes
([simulavr/Dockerfile](simulavr/Dockerfile)): a few minutes, most of it
downloading prind's Klipper tools image (1.6 GB to download, about 5.5 GB on
disk with the built image). Klipper reports `ready` some
seconds after the containers start:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7130/printer/info
```

Print the keys as shell exports (`JP_MOONRAKER_KEY`, `JP_OCTOPRINT_KEY`, and a
wrong one, `JP_BAD_KEY`):

```bash
eval "$(tests/printer_hosts/keys.sh)"
```

OctoPrint's key is fixed in `docker-compose.yml`. Moonraker makes its own key
on first start and keeps it until the volumes are removed. OctoPrint's web page
signs in as `admin` / `jusprin-test`.

```bash
docker compose -f tests/printer_hosts/docker-compose.yml down       # keeps keys and uploaded files
docker compose -f tests/printer_hosts/docker-compose.yml down -v    # back to a first start
```

The simulated board uses most of a CPU core for as long as it runs, so stop the
stack when you are done.

## Connecting a printer in the app

Use a printer that is not made by Bambu Lab, such as the generic Klipper
printer, and give the app an address from the table above, with
Moonraker or OctoPrint as the host type. When the app asks for an API key, type
the one `keys.sh` prints, a wrong one, or none, depending on the case. Each
address answers the way a real host does:

| Address and key | What the app's connection test gets |
|---|---|
| `7130`, no key | accepted; Klipper is ready |
| `7131` or `5030`, no key or a wrong key | refused (HTTP 401 or 403), so the app asks for a key |
| `7131` or `5030`, the right key | accepted |

## States worth testing

- **Ready, printing, paused, cancelled, complete:** send G-code with the app,
  or through the API (`/server/files/upload` with `print=true`,
  `/printer/print/pause`, `/printer/print/cancel`). The simulated Klipper
  board runs at half speed (see [simulavr/Dockerfile](simulavr/Dockerfile)),
  so its prints take twice their estimate: the app's 20 mm cube on the
  generic Klipper printer, estimated at 10 minutes, takes about 20.
  OctoPrint's virtual printer keeps its own pace.

OctoPrint's virtual printer keeps its own pace.
- **Klipper shut down behind a working Moonraker:** `docker compose … stop simulavr`.
  Moonraker then reports Klipper's state as `shutdown`, "Lost communication
  with MCU 'mcu'", as a real printer whose board has dropped off does. Start
  `simulavr` again, then restart `klipper` (a `FIRMWARE_RESTART` cannot reset
  the simulated board).
- **Host offline:** stop the Moonraker or OctoPrint container.
- **Nothing listening:** any other port, such as `7139`.
- **Wrong host type:** OctoPrint at `7130` (Moonraker answers OctoPrint's API
  through its `[octoprint_compat]` section, so this connects), or Moonraker at
  `5030` (HTTP 404).

## Cameras

Each printer has a camera, served by [go2rtc](https://github.com/AlexxIT/go2rtc)
in the `camera` container. A camera films a test pattern labelled with its
printer and a clock (UTC), so a frozen feed is easy to spot. Open these in a
browser on the same computer:

| Printer | Live feed (MJPEG) | One picture (JPEG) |
|---|---|---|
| Klipper, both Moonrakers | `http://127.0.0.1:7140/api/stream.mjpeg?src=klipper` | `http://127.0.0.1:7140/api/frame.jpeg?src=klipper` |
| OctoPrint | `http://127.0.0.1:7140/api/stream.mjpeg?src=octoprint` | `http://127.0.0.1:7140/api/frame.jpeg?src=octoprint` |

The hosts hand out the same addresses, as real ones do:

- Moonraker lists the camera at `/server/webcams/list`, from the `[webcam printer]`
  section of [open.conf](moonraker/open.conf) and [key.conf](moonraker/key.conf).
- OctoPrint shows it on its Control tab, and lists it in `/api/settings` under
  `plugins.classicwebcam`. Every start sets it from `WEBCAM_STREAM` and
  `WEBCAM_SNAPSHOT` in `docker-compose.yml`.

These addresses work only on this computer. OctoPrint's server also fetches the
picture address itself, for timelapses, and inside its container `127.0.0.1`
is not this computer, so that fetch fails.

The feeds run at 10 frames a second. A camera's ffmpeg runs only while
something is watching it, so cameras nobody watches cost nothing.

To test a camera that is offline: `docker compose … stop camera`. The hosts
keep listing the camera, but its address no longer answers.

If your stack was started before the cameras were added, run `down` and then
`up -d` (without `-v`) once, so the hosts reload their settings.

## The printer

`klipper/printer.cfg` matches the app's generic Klipper printer (MyKlipper 0.4
nozzle: 250 × 250 × 250, 0.4 mm nozzle, 1.75 mm filament) and defines the
`PRINT_START` and `PRINT_END` macros its start and end G-code call, so that
printer's G-code prints unchanged. simulavr's endstops always read as pressed
and its thermistors read about 103 °C, so homing sets the position without
moving, and M109/M190 set a temperature without waiting for it. Status reports
the target temperatures, but the measured ones stay near 103 °C.

## With the shell harness

`--print-host-check` takes a file of cases, one per line, and runs the app's
connection tool on each without a model:

```
moonraker http://127.0.0.1:7130
moonraker http://127.0.0.1:7131 JP_MOONRAKER_KEY
octoprint http://127.0.0.1:5030 JP_BAD_KEY
```

Export the keys first, as above.

## Versions

Every image is pinned. `KLIPPER_TAG` in [.env](.env) picks the
`mkuf/klipper` tag for both Klipper and the simulated board, whose firmware is
built from that tag's `-tools` image, so the two always match. After changing
it, rebuild with `docker compose … build simulavr`. The cameras are
`alexxit/go2rtc:1.9.14`.

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation. Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, Bash, Edit, Read, SendUserFile, ToolSearch, Write, mcp__ccd_session__start_session, mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__list_sessions, mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__search_session_transcripts, mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan, mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up, mcp__computer-use__app_batch, mcp__computer-use__app_bring_to_current_space, mcp__computer-use__app_click, mcp__computer-use__app_list_windows, mcp__computer-use__app_release, mcp__computer-use__app_screenshot, mcp__computer-use__app_zoom, mcp__computer-use__request_access Summary: 1. **Primary Request and Intent** **Earlier work in this session, finished:** - Live-tested the agent's Moonraker setup. - Found the root cause of the Home printer card's false "Idle": a state field defaults to Idle and only Bambu sets it. - Surveyed every printer connection type and proposed one status list: Not connected, Connecting…, Connected, Ready, Printing, Paused, Needs attention. - Drew boards on the design canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ, Main Page, row at y=2960). Kenneth had the camera put back on them. - Kenneth decided there is no collapsed or one-line card. In his words: "determine if each of those fields need to show. And let the card naturally grow or shrink." - I produced the rule for when each card field shows, per connection type, in `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/cf7649d3-46dd-4047-a831-32851ae18292/scratchpad/report/printer-card-fields-by-connection.md`, sent it to Kenneth, and asked which printers' readings to build first. **Kenneth's latest message (verbatim):** - Quoting my line "Camera: only while the printer is printing or paused, and only if the app has a stream for that printer.", he wrote: "Let's make it always on as long as the stream is available." - "Moonraker, then bambu" **Current task:** implement Moonraker first. That means reading Klipper's activity, job, progress, time left, message, camera and last print result, and showing them on a redesigned Home card that grows and shrinks with its fields, under the agreed rules. The camera now shows whenever a stream is available. Bambu's fields come after Moonraker. 2. **Key Technical Concepts** - JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer (C++/wxWidgets). The Home page is React (HomeUI) in a web view, talking to native code over a bridge (`window.__jusprinBridge.deliver`, `window.wx.postMessage`). - `HostReadings` / `HostLaneReader` poll each print host every 10 s on a thread. A reading stays fresh for 30 s. - Moonraker endpoints the poll now uses: - `printer/objects/query?webhooks&print_stats&display_status`. It answers 200 even while Klipper is shut down. It answers 503 when Klippy is disconnected; this 503 claim is not yet verified. - `server/history/list?limit=1&order=desc`. Its newest job carries `metadata.estimated_time`. - `server/webcams/list`. - Unchanged: `server/database/item?namespace=lane_data` and `printer/objects/query?mmu`. - Time left is computed: estimated_time − print_duration. - Upstream's Moonraker agent announces the selected print host as its own device, with dev_id equal to the saved address. That produced a duplicate "127.0.0.1:7130" card on Home. - Design-token rule: every UI value comes from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json` through CSS variables, guarded by `styles.test.ts` and `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp`. - Shared-Mac build rules: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, build with `-j4`, run one build per build directory, start the build in its own process group with `perl setpgrp`. 3. **Files and Code Sections** All paths below are under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `tests/` or `resources/`. - **`Printers/HostLanes.hpp`** (the readings header) - Header comment now covers activity, job and camera. - New types and functions: - `struct KlipperState { klippy, klippy_message, print, filename, message, print_duration, std::optional progress }`. - `parse_klipper_state(body)`. - `struct HostJob { filename, status, estimated_time, end_time }` and `parse_last_job(body)`. - `struct HostCamera { stream_url, snapshot_url }` and `parse_webcams(body, web_origin)`. - `enum class HostActivity { Ready, Printing, Paused, Starting, KlipperDown }` and `host_activity(const KlipperState&)`. - `HostReading` and `HostStatus` gain `klipper`, `last_job` and `camera`. - `HostStatus` gains `std::optional last_answered`. - `HostReadings` gains `using Wall = std::chrono::system_clock`, and `finish(..., Wall::time_point wall = Wall::now())` and `note_answered(..., wall = Wall::now())`. - `Entry` gains `answered_wall`, `klipper`, `last_job` and `camera`. - **`Printers/HostLanes.cpp`** (the parsers) - New helpers: `number_field`, `result_of`, and `camera_url`. - `camera_url` resolves a relative path against the host's scheme and name with the port dropped, because Mainsail serves cameras from nginx on port 80. - `parse_klipper_state`: - Requires a `webhooks` object; without one it returns nullopt. - Keeps only the first line of `state_message`. - Clamps `progress` to 0..1. - `parse_last_job` reads `jobs[0]`. - `parse_webcams` returns the first enabled camera. - It keeps a stream URL only for services "", "mjpegstreamer" and "uv4l-mjpeg"; any other service gets its snapshot only. - It returns nullopt when a camera has neither URL. - `host_activity`: - "startup" gives Starting. - Any other non-"ready" state gives KlipperDown. - Otherwise printing gives Printing, paused gives Paused, and anything else gives Ready. - `status()` copies klipper, last_job, camera and last_answered. `finish()` stores them. - **`Printers/HostLaneReader.cpp`** - After `reached = true`, the reader calls a new `read_activity(reading)`: ```cpp const auto [status, body] = get("printer/objects/query?webhooks&print_stats&display_status"); if (status == 200) reading.klipper = parse_klipper_state(body); else if (status == 503) reading.klipper = KlipperState{"disconnected"}; if (const auto [hs, hb] = get("server/history/list?limit=1&order=desc"); hs == 200) reading.last_job = parse_last_job(hb); if (const auto [ws, wb] = get("server/webcams/list"); ws == 200) reading.camera = parse_webcams(wb, make_url("")); ``` - The duplicate `private:` was removed so `read_activity` and `get` share one private section. - The header comment in `HostLaneReader.hpp` was updated to match. - **`Home/HomeSnapshot.hpp`** (the card's data) - `PrinterState` and `ConnectionState` are gone. New enums, each with a `to_string`: - `PrinterStatus { NotConnected, Connecting, Connected, Ready, Printing, Paused, NeedsAttention }` - `LastPrint { Unknown, Finished, Failed, Cancelled }` - `PrinterAction { None, Monitor, PrinterWindow, Reconnect, Connect }` - `PrinterEntry` fields: - Kept: id, name, kind, can_open_settings, can_rename, can_remove, spools, history. - New: `status`, `job`, `progress_percent{-1}`, `seconds_left{-1}`, `message`, `last_print`, `last_connected_at` (ISO 8601), `camera_stream_url`, `camera_snapshot_url`, `connection_label`, `action`. - `address` and `model_text` stay, and are now parts of the facts line. - **`Home/HomeSnapshot.cpp`** (turns the card into JSON) - `printer_json` always sends id, name, kind, status, spools, action and the three menu flags. - Only when set, it sends job and message. - `progressPercent` and `secondsLeft` are sent only while printing, paused or needing attention. - `lastPrint` is sent only when the status is ready. - `lastConnectedAt` is sent only when the status is not_connected. - `camera {streamUrl?, snapshotUrl?}`, connectionLabel, address, modelText and history are sent when present. - Wire strings: - Status: "not_connected", "connecting", "connected", "ready", "printing", "paused", "attention". - Action: "none", "monitor", "printer_window", "reconnect", "connect". - Last print: "finished", "failed", "cancelled". - **`Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp`** (builds the cards) - Removed `remaining_text`; the page now words the time left. - `describe_device` (Bambu): - Recent data gives connection_label "LAN" or "Cloud" and action Monitor. A printing machine gives Printing, or Paused when `print_status == "PAUSE"`, with the percent and seconds left. Otherwise Ready. - A silent printer gives Not connected, with the message "The printer stopped sending updates." and Reconnect, but only for a named printer whose connection was verified. A device card no longer gets the Reconnect that failed with "no longer exists". - New helpers: - `host_label(config)`: "Klipper" for Moonraker, "OctoPrint" for OctoPrint, otherwise Orca's own enum label. - `iso_utc(...)`. - `job_name(filename)`: strips the folder and the .gcode/.gco/.g/.bgcode extension. - New `describe_host(status, printer)`: - Checking gives Connecting with no button. - Unreachable gives Not connected, "%s isn't answering.", Reconnect, and last_connected_at. - Reachable starts as Connected with Open printer window, and copies the camera. Then, from Klipper's state: - Starting gives Connecting. - KlipperDown gives Not connected, with "Klipper stopped: " or "Klipper isn't running.", plus last_connected_at. - Printing or Paused gives the job, the percent, and the seconds left. Seconds left are computed only when the last job is in_progress with the same filename, an estimate above zero, and print_duration above zero. The message is print_stats.message. - Ready gives Ready, with last print completed→Finished, cancelled→Cancelled, in_progress or empty→Unknown, and anything else→Failed. - Named-printer loop: - Starts at Not connected with "No network connection is set up." and Connect. - A saved print host sets connection_label and address, clears that message, and adds both the raw print_host and the address to `represented`, which removes the duplicate device card. - Then `describe_host`. - With a Bambu device present, it clears the message and button, then calls `describe_device`. If the result is Not connected with no button, it offers Connect. Monitor marks the connection verified. - A verified but absent device gives Not connected, "The printer stopped sending updates." and Reconnect. - Host lanes show only when the card is not Not connected. - `settle_connection` was removed. - **`Shell/SetupCommands.hpp` and `.cpp`** (the header menu's state) - `ConnectionState` is now `{NotConnected, Ready, Printing, Paused, Connected, Offline, Checking}`; Idle is renamed Ready. - A new `host_state(const HostStatus&)` maps Klipper's activity: no Klipper state gives Connected, Starting gives Checking, KlipperDown gives Offline. - Bambu PAUSE now gives Paused. - **`Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp`** - Machine row: Ready is "Ready" with a positive tone. New Paused (warning) and Connected (neutral) cases. - `other_printer` is rewritten around `Home::PrinterStatus`, using the same words as the card. - **`HomeUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts`** - New types: `PrinterStatus`, `LastPrint`, `PrinterAction`, `PrinterCamera`. - `PrinterInfo` now has status, job?, progressPercent?, secondsLeft?, message?, lastPrint?, lastConnectedAt?, camera?, connectionLabel?, address?, modelText?, spools and action. - `PrinterState` and `ConnectionState` are removed. - **`HomeUI/src/components/PrinterCard.tsx`** (rewritten) - Exports `timeLeft`, `statusDetail` and `lastConnected`. - The `Camera` component shows an `` of the stream, or the snapshot with `&t=` or `?t=` refreshed every 2000 ms. It removes itself on error. It carries a LIVE tag with a status dot. - Card order: camera, head (glyph, name, menu), status (dot unless not_connected or connecting, the word, " · detail"), job, progress (class follows the status), message, "since" line, facts (label · address · model), spools, history, button. - `PrinterChip` is removed. The component takes an optional `now` prop for tests. - **`HomeUI/src/App.tsx`** - Removed `startsCollapsed`, the opened-chip state and its effect, the PrinterChip import, and the unused PrinterInfo import. - Every printer now renders as a `PrinterCard`. - **`HomeUI/src/styles.css`** - New status-dot classes: ready (success), paused (warning), attention (danger), connected (text-tertiary). result.output: Web search results for query: "img tag MJPEG stream connection lost onerror not fired last frame frozen Safari WebKit" Links: [{"title":"Closed Bug 1151309 Opened 9 years ago Closed 9 years ago","url":"https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1151309"},{"title":"show bug","url":"https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=599975"},{"title":"show bug","url":"https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=987135"},{"title":"show bug","url":"https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=858600"},{"title":"mjpeg html5 video doesn t stream with video","url":"https://kiwix.lema.org/stackoverflow.com_en_all_2023-11/questions/37239869/mjpeg-html5-video-doesn-t-stream-with-video"},{"title":"mjpg does not work in Safari/Chrome (iOS also)","url":"https://forum.felenasoft.com/viewtopic.php?p=3358"},{"title":"how to detect when mjpeg stream stops with javascript","url":"https://kiwix.lema.org/stackoverflow.com_en_all_2023-11/questions/67204268/how-to-detect-when-mjpeg-stream-stops-with-javascript"}] The search didn't turn up a WebKit bug report that matches this exact symptom, so these are community reports and related browser bugs rather than confirmed root causes. - **Known pattern:** Several sources describe an `` MJPEG stream freezing on the last frame. One Stack Overflow answer says the only events you get from an `img` element are load, error, and abort, and that's the limit of what's available. There is no general support for MJPEG streams in any browser beyond the img element. The closest we get to monitor events with the img element is to listen to the onload, onerror and onabort events. - **Safari and iOS reports:** A Xeoma forum thread says it will play the stream and after 5-10 seconds it will FREEZE on iOS 9. The same thread notes the animation problem returned in later Safari and Chrome versions. - **Why `onerror` may not fire:** A Firefox bug report says a stream can stop without any error being raised, and a related one notes that an empty `src` may produce no error event in some browsers. Neither is a Safari-specific finding. - **Workaround that users report:** In a Stack Overflow thread, one user found that in Safari document.readyState will change from interactive to complete. Another user checks whether the image has stopped loading on a timer, after the `onload` event fires on each frame. A third suggests wrapping the stream in an iframe, which reportedly fires repeated load events in Safari but not in Chrome. For a reliable stop detector in Safari, a watchdog timer that tracks the time since the last `load` event is probably the most practical option. I'd also check the WebKit bug tracker directly for a Safari-specific report before relying on any of these workarounds. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

Both pages find their host through `window.wx.postMessage(json)` and receive host
envelopes through `window.__jusprinBridge.deliver(envelope)` (`WebShared/bridgeClient.ts`).
Copy `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` to a scratch dir, inject

`hello_ack` + a full `state`, and (2) exposes `window.fake.deliver(type, payload)`;
serve with `python3 -m http.server` and open `agent.html?panel=printer` /
`home.html` via `preview_start`. Drive it with `javascript_tool`: deliver
`assistant_started` with no `assistant_delta` to freeze a streaming empty turn,
`printer_session` to pin a card, `printer_added` for Home's receipt strip. A file
drop works with `new DragEvent('drop', {dataTransfer})` on `.app--printer`.
Envelope: `{protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge'|'jusprin-home-bridge', version:1, id, type, payload}`.

`app_click` never reaches WKWebView content, so page-level states (streaming

proof. It proves page rendering only; host behaviour (e.g. the 256 KiB image
preview cap `kInlineImagePreviewCap` in `AgentHost.cpp`) must be replicated in
the fake by hand or checked live.
