# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)

Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.

Moonraker and OctoPrint printers run against the real host software in Docker
([print hosts README](../../../../../tests/printer_hosts/README.md)). Do not
add a Bambu network fake unless asked.

This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.

## What success looks like

- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.

If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.

## Turn it on

Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.

`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:

```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```

JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.

Keep a **Bambu Lab printer** selected: a real system preset, typically
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`, or a named printer that inherits one.
`is_bbl_vendor()` must be true; it reads the inherited `printer_model`, so
either works. An embedded 3mf preset named
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough; the agent stays
`orca`.

**Add a printer…** in the printer menu installs the system preset and saves it
as a named printer (a user profile such as `Bambu Lab A1 mini`), which is what
Home lists. Alternatively copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into
`<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to the `models` array in
`JusPrin2.conf`, then select the system preset. Opening
`~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps after that vendor is installed.

Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
config. JusPrin turns `single_instance` on at every start; its instance lock
lives in the data directory, so a scratch `--datadir` runs as its own instance
beside another JusPrin. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.

The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.

For an MCP client, the shell harness does all of this in its own datadir:
`shell_integration_harness --manual-mcp <dir> --fake-printer` saves a
**Fake A1 mini** printer, connects it to the fake and selects it before it
prints `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY`. Edits to the conf would not survive: the
fixture rewrites it at startup.

## Drive state

Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
fake rereads it about once a second.

```json
{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
| `spools` | loaded AMS spools; see below. Absent leaves whatever was last set |

No `spools` (or an empty array) reports no AMS at all, same as before this
field existed. A non-empty array reports one AMS unit (id `"0"`) with one
tray per spool, up to 4:

```json
{"spools": [{"subBrands": "PLA Matte", "trayType": "PLA", "colour": "5F7D4FFF"}]}
```

`subBrands` is what `PrinterDiscovery.cpp` reads back as the spool's name
when set (ahead of `trayType`), so it is the field worth setting for a
saved/network-printer card or receipt to show something. `trayType` is the
spool's material (Home's Loaded row names it); the fake sends it beside a
`tray_info_idx`, since upstream ignores a type that arrives without one.
`filamentId` sets that id (`"GFA01"` is Bambu PLA Matte); left out, the
id is empty, and Orca's filament sync skips the tray. `colour` is optional: a spool without it reports no colour, and Home
draws no swatch for it.

Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.

## Print

Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.

If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
scenario after send.

## Isolate a running app (agents)

Another JusPrin may already be open. Do not send keys or clicks to it.

On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or by
a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto'd `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`).
`osascript` `unix id` filters can match the wrong process; prefer
`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` or the unique bundle id.

Keyboard events posted to the pid work while the Mac is locked; mouse events
posted that way do not. Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer
half of the chip is a wx control (`SetName("Printer")`) and often has no AX
title; click by coordinates after a screenshot, or use the documented shortcut
for Print.

Logs: `<datadir>/log/debug_*.log`. This machine's default `grep` may be ugrep;
use `/usr/bin/grep -a` on app logs.

## A real printer, no model

The printer tools are not exposed over MCP, so `probe.call` cannot reach them.
`shell_integration_harness --printer-network-check <dir> <address> <version>`
drives them with a scripted stand-in for the model, on Bambu's real plug-in:
copy `plugins/` from a data folder that has it into `<dir>` first, and pass the
version in its `libbambu_networking_<version>.dylib` name. It expects a P1S in
cloud mode at `<address>`, prints each tool result and note as
`HARNESS NETWORK` lines, and sends the printer nothing. `--simulate-announce` after
the version hands the app that announcement itself 25 seconds in, for when no
printer is on; it tests everything after the plug-in, not the plug-in. Printers announce on UDP
2021. While another program holds that port the plug-in hears nothing, and
`printer_connection_status` reports `port_taken`, so quit whatever
`lsof -nP -iUDP:2021` names first. The plug-in takes the port only as the app
starts, so once that program lets go the status reports `not_listening` until a
restart. Holding the port from a small script is how to test both states.

`--printer-connect-skill <dir> <address> <version>` runs the same chats for
the connection skill; pass `none` as the version to run without the plug-in.
`--open-issue` after the version also calls `issue_report_open`, which opens
the default browser on a filled-in GitHub issue page. Nothing is filed unless
someone presses Submit there, so close the tab. That run keeps its data
folder; the link is in `log/debug_*.log` under "opening an issue page".

`jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (Catch2, GUI build). They cover announce JSON,
control-file parsing, and agent id. They do not start the heartbeat unless the
test sets `set_queue_on_main_fn`.

The search confirms the code's meaning but doesn't identify a cause or fix.

- **Meaning:** Bambu's community error-code list maps 0300400C to "Printing was cancelled." The decimal value 50348044 is the same code (0x0300400C), so the two forms refer to one error.
- **Common reports:** Several users in the "Print Cancelled, but why and by what?" forum thread describe the same message on P1-series printers, often on long prints. Some say the printer was still moving when the app reported cancellation. One user suggested making other error-handling instead of the 'cancelled print' error-handling.
- **Suspected causes:** Posters have blamed SD cards, slicer versions, and firmware. One user downgraded their firmware and didn't have the issue again, but others reported it recurring on older firmware. A forum post about an A1 with this code says "I found the code, but not the answer."
- **Support:** Bambu Lab support has responded in that thread, and a user reported opening a ticket with logs and the 3MF file.

No official Bambu explanation or confirmed fix appeared in these results. The most useful next steps are checking the HMS/history log for the events leading up to the cancel, noting firmware and slicer versions, and opening a support ticket with logs.

content.text:
Home's printer cards now show what each Klipper or Bambu printer reports instead of a bare "Idle". Each card has its status, the job, the percent and time left, the printer's own message, when it was last connected, and how the last print ended. A Klipper card shows its camera whenever the camera answers, as you asked. Nothing is committed.

**What I tested**

- **Klipper:** I ran the app on the Docker test printer and stepped it through each state. The cards read:
  - Printing: "Printing · 4% · 14m left", with the job name.
  - Paused: "Paused · at 5%".
  - Ended: "Ready · last print cancelled" or "Ready · last print finished".
  - Board shut down: "Klipper stopped: Lost communication with MCU 'mcu'".
  - Klipper stopped: "Klipper isn't running."
  - Pi off: "127.0.0.1:7130 isn't answering." with Reconnect.
  - The extra "127.0.0.1:7130" card that used to sit beside the named printer is gone.
- **Bambu:** I tested against the fake Bambu printer, in six new harness checks. They all pass.
  - A printer that pauses on an error reads "Needs attention" with Bambu's message for the error.
  - A pause without an error reads "Paused".
  - A printing card names the job.
  - After a print ends, the card says whether it finished, failed or was cancelled.
- **Automated tests:**
  - Native tests: 200 pass.
  - Home page tests: 123 pass.
  - Fake Bambu printer tests: 14 pass.
  - Every print-host and Home card check in the shell harness passes.

**Problems found while testing, now fixed**

- **Frozen camera:** In the app's web view, a camera stream that stops raises no error. The image just keeps its last frame, still labelled LIVE; I watched it do this for 30 seconds. The card now asks the camera for one picture every 5 seconds. The camera comes off the card about 6 seconds after it stops, and comes back with the stream reconnected about 5 seconds after it returns.
- **"Last connected just now":** This showed on a printer whose Klipper had been down for minutes, because the Pi kept answering. It now gives the last time Klipper itself was up.
- **Cut-off facts line:** The line with the connection type, address and model was cut off with "…", which hid the model and nozzle. It now wraps.

**Still open**

- **Bambu camera:** Bambu printers don't offer a camera address the page can show. Upstream plays their cameras through its own native player, so Bambu cards have no camera yet. The question box asks whether to build a native bridge for them now.
- **Harness failures outside this change:**
  - The harness's printer-setup run stops early on a nozzle-panel check, at a project folder that doesn't exist. I skipped that section temporarily to reach the printer checks, then put the file back exactly as it was.
  - Three checks also fail because closing the setup panel during a connection test still saves the late answer.
  - My change doesn't touch either code path, but I haven't run them against an unchanged build to prove they failed before.
- **Design System artifact:** The new design token, a camera height of 135, still needs adding there.

I sent a picture of the real Home page drawing five of these cards.

Sources for the Bambu cancel code (0300400C means "Printing was cancelled"): [Bambu forum, error code list](https://forum.bambulab.com/t/poll-bambu-lab-please-provide-a-complete-list-of-error-codes/17232/7), [Bambu forum, 0300-400C](https://forum.bambulab.com/t/printing-was-cancelled-0300-400c-1330/88015/3). On camera streams freezing without an error: [Stack Overflow, detecting when an MJPEG stream stops](https://kiwix.lema.org/stackoverflow.com_en_all_2023-11/questions/67204268/how-to-detect-when-mjpeg-stream-stops-with-javascript).

1. **Primary Request and Intent**
   - **Earlier work, finished:**
     - Found why the Home card said "Idle" for a printer that wasn't idle.
     - Proposed one status list: Not connected, Connecting…, Connected, Ready, Printing, Paused, Needs attention.

     - Kenneth decided there is no collapsed card: each field shows only when it applies, and the card grows or shrinks.
     - I wrote the rule for when each field shows. It is in `scratchpad/report/printer-card-fields-by-connection.md`.
   - **Kenneth's latest message:** quoting my line "Camera: only while the printer is printing or paused, and only if the app has a stream for that printer.", he wrote "Let's make it always on as long as the stream is available." and then "Moonraker, then bambu".
   - **What that means:** implement the Moonraker card fields first, then Bambu's.

2. **Key Technical Concepts**
   - JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer. The Home page is React (HomeUI) running in a web view and talks to native code over a bridge.
   - `HostReadings` and `HostLaneReader` poll each print host every 10 seconds. A reading counts as fresh for 30 seconds.
   - Moonraker endpoints the poll uses:
     - `printer/objects/query?webhooks&print_stats&display_status`. It answers 503 "Klippy Host not connected" when Klipper itself is stopped (verified live).
     - `server/history/list?limit=1&order=desc`
     - `server/webcams/list`
   - Bambu fields come from `MachineObject`:
     - `print_status` is one of FINISH, RUNNING, PAUSE, FAILED, PREPARE.
     - `print_error`, `subtask_name`, `mc_print_percent`, `mc_left_time`.
     - `GetHMS()->GetHMSItems()` gives the printer's current health messages.
     - Text lookups: `HMSQuery::query_print_error_msg`, `query_hms_msg`, `is_internal_error`.
     - 0x0300400C (50348044) means "The task was canceled." This was confirmed on Bambu's forum and in `resources/hms/hms_en_*.json`.
   - The macOS web view fires no error when an MJPEG stream stops; the image keeps its last frame (verified with an in-page probe). So the card asks the camera for one picture every 5 seconds, out of sight.
   - Shared-Mac build rules: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, build with `-j4`, run one build per build folder, and start each build in its own process group with `perl setpgrp`.

3. **Files and Code Sections** (changes in this stretch, all uncommitted on jusprin-newui)
   - **`Printers/HostLanes.hpp` and `.cpp`**
     - `HostStatus::last_answered` is renamed `last_connected`. It now means the host answered and, behind Moonraker, Klipper was up.
     - `Entry::answered_wall` is renamed `connected_wall`.
     - `finish()` sets `connected_wall` only when there is no Klipper state, or Klipper's activity is neither KlipperDown nor Starting.
     - `note_answered(key, now)` lost its wall-clock parameter and no longer sets the time.
   - **`Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp`**
     - Uses `status.last_connected`.
     - Includes `DeviceCore/DevHMS.h` and `HMS.hpp`.
     - `job_name` also strips `.gcode.3mf` and `.3mf`.
     - `describe_device` now sits after `job_name`. New pieces:
       - `constexpr int kBambuPrintCancelled = 0x0300400C;`
       - `has_print_error(machine)`: print_error is above 0, is not the cancel code, and is not one Bambu marks internal.
       - `device_message(machine)`: the job's error text, otherwise the first fatal or serious health message. If the app has no text, it says "The printer reports error %s."
       - While printing: the job is set from `subtask_name`. When paused, the message is set, and a job error makes the status NeedsAttention.
       - Not printing: Ready, with FINISH giving Finished, and FAILED giving Cancelled for the cancel code and Failed otherwise.
   - **`HomeUI/src/components/PrinterCard.tsx`**
     - New exported `CAMERA_CHECK_EVERY_MS = 5000` and a `fresh(url, tick)` helper.
     - `Camera` keeps the answering state in both state and a ref. A `connection` counter is bumped on recovery and used as the img `key`, so the stream reconnects.
     - Every 5 seconds the card checks the camera with `new Image()` on the snapshot URL, or the stream URL if there is no snapshot. Settling a check clears its handlers and sets `src=''`.
     - A check still unanswered at the next check counts as not answering.
     - The camera is hidden while it is not answering.
     - `statusDetail` gives "at N%" for attention as well as paused.
   - **`PrinterCard.test.tsx`**: two camera tests that stub `Image` with `vi.stubGlobal`, plus an attention detail case. Both camera tests were shown to fail with the check switched off.
   - **`HomeUI/src/styles.css`**: `.printer-facts` now wraps (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`) instead of cutting off with an ellipsis.
   - **`Testing/FakeBambuAgent.hpp` and `.cpp`**:
     - `FakeBambuStatusStep::print_error`.
     - The control file's `print_error` defaults to 0 when left out.
     - `push_status` sends `print_error`.
   - **`Testing/README.md`**: documents `print_error` (117473297 = 0x07008011 for a pause needing attention; 50348044 for cancelled).
   - **`tests/jusprin/test_host_lanes.cpp`**: tests `last_connected`, including that a Klipper shutdown does not move it.
   - **`tests/jusprin/test_fake_bambu_agent.cpp`**: new test "FakeBambuAgent control JSON reports the job's error code while it is set".
   - **`tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`**:
     - New `BambuJobCase` struct and `verify_home_bambu_job(name, control, index, then)`, run after the tray checks in `verify_home_bambu_card`.
     - Six cases, with an each-tick note that prints what the card reads.

   - **Memory** `printer-status-one-list-boards.md` records what was built and what is still open.

4. **Errors and fixes**

   - `docker compose stop` silently did nothing. I used `docker stop <container>` instead.
   - The cards page lost its styles because the bundle applies its CSS from script. I used a fixture page with a stand-in host and Playwright instead. Playwright can only save files under the repo's `.playwright-mcp` folder, so I moved the pictures out and deleted the folder.

input.command:
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Printer cards: one status, and show each field only when the printer reports it

Home's printer cards said "Idle" for a Moonraker printer whose Klipper was
shut down, because the state field defaulted to Idle and only Bambu set it.
Each card now has one status (Not connected, Connecting..., Connected,
Ready, Printing, Paused, Needs attention) and shows each field -- job,
progress, the printer's message, "Last connected ...", camera, last print
outcome -- only when the printer reports it, so the card grows and shrinks.

Moonraker: the 10-second host poll also reads Klipper's state, the newest
history entry and the webcam list. A 503 from Moonraker means Klipper itself
is not running. "Last connected" is the last reading with Klipper up, not
merely the Pi answering.

Bambu: the job name comes from subtask_name; a pause with a job error reads
Needs attention with the app's text for the error (or the code when the app
has none); a finished, failed or cancelled (0x0300400C) print shows on a
Ready card. No Bambu camera yet: it needs a native stream bridge.

Camera: shown whenever it answers. The macOS web view raises no error when
an MJPEG stream stops, so the card asks for one picture every 5 seconds and
takes a camera that does not answer off the card, reconnecting it when it
answers again.

The header's printer menu uses the same statuses. The fake Bambu printer's
control file gains print_error, and the shell harness checks six job states
against it.
EOF
git log --oneline -1 && git status --short

The one big exception is the credits, first-run and sign-in work, which I haven't merged because another session owns it and was active today. I've asked that session whether its work is finished, and I'll start on the failing tests and the connection-skill checks once the merge question is settled.

**How I checked**

There are about 190 local branches. Most are experiments from 2024 and 2025 that git can no longer merge cleanly. For the branches from the last three weeks, I checked whether their features exist on jusprin-newui. The prompt cache work, the Anthropic and OpenRouter providers, the journey harness, the slice-failure reasons and the history guard are all already there.

**The one piece not on jusprin-newui**

The credits, first-run and sign-in work isn't on jusprin-newui at all. It's 19 commits on `claude/elated-sutherland-84a741`, about 7,900 lines across 116 files. It covers:

- JusPrin Cloud credits and the balance panel
- the first-launch Welcome, then Printers, then Home flow
- signing in by email through allauth, the Django sign-in library behind the website
- Continue with Google
- signing in to jusprinv2.obico.io

Two other branches hold earlier stages of the same work, so merging this one covers them.

It belongs to [Use a JusPrin syndicate sharing accounts with Obico](#local_69a34677-cdae-4851-90bb-557cd0ba6d32), which was working on it about 15 minutes before I checked. I've asked that session three things:

- whether the work is finished
- whether it has uncommitted changes
- whether it wants to merge the work itself or have me do it

If I do it, my plan is to squash it into a few commits, one per feature, on top of jusprin-newui. Merging will conflict with today's printer card commit in the Home page files and the shell harness, and I'll resolve those conflicts.

**The two follow-ups you asked for**

- **The three failing tests:** none of the session reports gave their names, so I've asked [Connect flow: try first, real result in the same turn](#local_06507b60-9017-40e0-a562-51c34bd5a1ae) for the test names, the failure output and anything it found about the cause.

Tell Kenneth if that matters for who uses jusprin-newui builds.
</cross-session-message>

==== 5c4831131b Add JusPrin Cloud credits and the first-run path on Home
The app now shows and spends JusPrin Cloud credits, and a new install starts
on Home with a first-run path. This is steps 0, 1, 2, 4 and 5 of the credits
plan on the app side. Step 3 (Chargebee, the served Account and pricing pages,
v1 carry-over) is not here. It needs the gateway change on tsd-enterprise
branch claude/credits-ledger.

Onboarding, ported from 8f4588beae and brought to the current boards:
- Home walks through the welcome, importing presets from an OrcaSlicer install,
  choosing a printer, and opening a project or the bundled example.
- save_onboarding passed const char* to AppConfig::set, which saved every field
  as "true". It now saves each value.
- "I don't have a printer here" refused on a fresh install, because no vendor
  was installed. It now installs Generic Klipper Printer and saves it under its
  own name, as normal printer setup does, so the chip shows no warning.
- The example opens handy_models/3DBenchy.drc. The earlier example file had
  three stacked objects, three filaments and a collision warning.
- An empty project is no longer listed on Home when its only history is
  printer, filament or process choices. A chat on an empty plate stays listed.
- The welcome-back window's kept-price box is hidden behind
  V1_PRICE_CARRIES_OVER until step 3 ships.

Credits:
- Model pickers show each model's price and are greyed once the person has sent
  a message in the chat. The account's balance shows as a ring with a hover
  panel, and the composer offers "Get more credits" when a message can't be paid
  for. A 402 from the gateway ends in a failed card.
- Turns the app starts itself send X-JusPrin-Request: note and run on Expert
  without changing the chat's model. RecordConversion turns one format's stored
  turn into the other's, the same bytes each time, so provider caches still hit.
- A Standard chat leaves out the picture tools and says so on the attachment
  row, with a "New Expert chat" button.

Cost and rewards:
- A turn that polls for its own slice is answered with busy, and the third
  refused poll ends the turn. The note turn that reports the slice still runs.
- Print history has a report form with a photo, and Home shows the credit line
  when signed in to the account.

Tests: AgentUI Vitest (651) and HomeUI Vitest (130) with tsc, jusprin_tests
(151), agent_bridge_tests (506), shell_theme_tests (14), brand_tokens_tests and
the shell harness default run (600 checks) and --fresh-example pass on macOS.
The real app ran the fresh-install example on an empty data folder, and three
live chats ran through a local gateway. Windows and Linux were not run.
tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp also fixes three harness defects on macOS that
were there before this work: a null title bar menu in --print-history, page
reads cut at about 1000 characters, and fake-printer control writes within one
second being ignored.


==== f3fd24e01f Apply the final credit rules in the app
Kenneth reviewed the credits boards and changed the rules. Every credit is now
the same, a balance is one number of credits, and the app stops translating it
into messages.

- The balance panel has one bar per lot, grouped by expiry, and bought credits
  get a bar too. Workshop's bar adds "Unused credits don't carry over."
- Prices in messages stay only on the model menu and the stop card. The
  first-month offer now reads "An Expert message is 5 credits. Your own API key
  stays free." Welcome-back reads "750 credits a month."
- The low-balance notice reads "About 25 credits left" at 25 credits or less on
  any model that charges, once, with Get more credits and a close button. The
  rounding to the nearest 5 is a fill-in, not Kenneth's.
- "New Standard chat" and "New Expert chat" are gone, along with the host's
  chatModel and draft path and the error details that fed them. A chat that
  cannot be paid offers Get more credits only.
- A picture in a Standard chat now shows as a warning on its chip, with Remove.
- A new chat on the account starts on Expert while a first-month lot is live and
  on Standard after it, as on board 6a. This was unbuilt until now.
- Standard has no thinking picker, because its alias now has no efforts.

Fixed along the way: the two-line rows in the model menu overlapped, because menu
rows have a fixed height. Vitest does not apply CSS, so a real-app screenshot
found it. No automated test guards it.

Not done: the pricing page, the savings alert and the Account switch belong to
later steps and are not built. Open bug: on a Standard chat the app can show
"The automatic chat title could not be generated", because the model sometimes
answers the message instead of writing a title (4 of 12 direct tries were too
long to use).

Tested: Agent page 654 tests, agent bridge 506, JusPrin 151. The real app ran
against a local gateway with real keys: 0, 1 and 5 credits charged as intended on
a file-opened turn, a Standard message and an Expert message. The shell harness
last ran before the low-balance and report-limit changes. Windows, Linux and dark
mode were not run.


==== e718eb7a76 Stop handling print reports that earn nothing
Kenneth removed the daily limit and the stop after invalid reports, so a report
always earns its 25 credits. The form's "earned no credits" screen, its two
sentences and its Done button can no longer be reached, and neither can the
noReward field carried from the gateway through the host to the page.

The gateway side of this is on claude/credits-ledger in tsd-enterprise; the two
go together.

Tested: Home page 129 tests, agent bridge 506, JusPrin 151. Not run in the real
app or the shell harness; a search of the harness found no use of what was
removed.


==== 15034337d2 Expect no project card for a chat on an empty plate in --fresh-example
jusprin-newui now keeps an empty project in memory until it holds a model, so
a chat on an empty plate no longer saves the project or lists it on Home. The
fresh-example harness check said the opposite and failed on the merged tree;
it now expects the project to stay unlisted. The mode exits 0 with this change.


==== 8062349956 Let Preferences close itself after one task and report how it ended
The first launch's "Your own API key" and "Claude Code or Claude
Desktop" doors open Preferences on its Agent section and need to know
whether the person finished. ShellController::open_preferences and
request_preferences now take an optional callback. When one is given,
the window is opened "for one task": the Preferences page closes it once
a key is verified, or once Done is pressed after connecting an AI tool,
and the callback receives "key" or "tool". If the person closes the
window first, the callback receives an empty string. A "key" only counts
when the agent is enabled in the app config.

reload_agent_settings() is split out of open_preferences so that Home's
browser sign-in can reload the docked agent the same way.

passed), and the shell harness in its default mode (failures=0).


==== 604683c151 Add a placeholder clip for the first-launch welcome screen
resources/jusprin/welcome/welcome-clip.mp4 is a PLACEHOLDER: the 12 s
stringing-Benchy animatic made for the value-proposition boards (620x388,
silent, 480 KB). The agent's words and setting values in it were typed
for the animatic, not recorded from the app. It is to be replaced by a
recording of the real app before release.

The clip shows two #3DBenchy photos licensed CC BY 2.0. The README in

==== 2e74fe2a3a Rewrite the first-launch controller as Welcome, then Printers, then Home
OnboardingModel now decides one of three things from the saved progress
(status, welcome_left, fresh_start, printer_chosen) and three facts (a
JusPrin v1 import, a printer that came with an opened file, printers in
an OrcaSlicer folder next to the data folder):

- Welcome shows on every first launch until any of its doors is used.
- Printers follows, unless the v1 import or an opened file already
  brought a printer. It offers OrcaSlicer's printers when there are
  some ("Import" or "Start fresh"); otherwise, or after Start fresh, it
  shows the add-printer form with "Skip, use a default", which installs
  Generic Klipper and marks that printer "assumed".
- Back on Printers returns to the welcome.
- Onboarding is saved as completed only once Home is reached. The
  earlier onboarding's "dismissed" status counts as completed, so nobody
  who dismissed it is welcomed again.

OrcaHomeBackend carries out the doors: the browser sign-in (CloudSignIn,
polled by a new 100 ms timer in HomeWebView), Preferences opened for one
task for the own-key and AI-tool doors, the OrcaSlicer import, and the
default printer. The add-printer form is the printer panel's own
PrinterConversation driven without model turns. The snapshot tells
Home's Agent group what to show: the three doors when no agent is set
up, or the account once after signing in.

Removed: the old steps and their messages (begin/dismiss, profile
bundle and folder choices, partial imports, manual setup wizard, the
example project), and the rule that hid the welcome once an agent was
configured.

Tested: jusprin_tests (153 cases, 840 assertions), agent_bridge_tests
(508), and JusPrinShellHarness in --fresh-example mode (40 checks, the
whole sequence: welcome, Just slice, Back, Start fresh, the catalogue
form, Skip, the assumed default printer, Home's doors) and in its
default mode (602 checks, failures=0).

Home's page now draws the boards on the "On boarding experience" canvas

Printers, and the add-printer form listed the real catalogue.


==== 5b0e3a9214 Let the JusPrin account sign in by email inside the app
CloudSignIn gains an Email phase beside the browser sign-in. The app
asks the server how an address signs in (POST /ent/jusprin/v2/auth/email):
an address with a password gets the password step, any other gets a
six-digit code by email. A correct code or password brings the same
OAuth token the browser sign-in brings, so it is checked and stored by
the same begin_check. A wrong or expired code, too many tries and a
wrong password stay on their step for the person to act on; any other
answer ends the sign-in with the generic "couldn't sign you in".

The HTTP post dependency passes 4xx bodies through so the refusal codes
reach the state machine. cloud_password_reset_url() names the server's
Forgot password page.


==== e005d55e62 Draw the sign-in door with Google and email on the welcome and Home
The welcome's sign-in card and Home's "Set up the agent" card share one
door: "Continue with Google" runs the browser sign-in, and an address
field with "Continue with email" runs the email sign-in. The server says
which step follows:

- a code: "Check your email." and six cells, the design system's
  Field/Verification Code, where the sixth digit signs in;
- a wrong or expired code: the cells outlined in danger, the reason,
  and "Send a new code";
- a password: "REDACTED", with "Email me a code instead" and
  "Forgot password", which opens the server's reset page.

The browser wait gains "Open the browser again" and "Use an email code
instead". The scale line reads "An Expert message is 5 credits. Your
own API key stays free.", and after a JusPrin v1 import the door adds
that v1 subscribers keep their original price. Terms and Privacy open
in the browser.

The free doors stay usable while a sign-in waits; only the check that
follows a token disables them. The code cell size is a new token,
component.onboarding.codeCell.


==== 69330fc5d9 Show what an OrcaSlicer import brought, item by item
Import on the Printers step used to ask yes or no in a dialog for each
name JusPrin already had, then said nothing about what it skipped. Now
a result screen follows it, one line per printer and process preset,
with the filaments counted:

- "Imported";
- "Imported as '<name> (Orca copy)'" when JusPrin had the name;
- "Not imported · <reason>": the file couldn't be read, has no version,
  isn't a preset, or names a base profile JusPrin lacks.

"Continue" leaves for Home, or for the add-printer form when no printer
came; "Retry failed items" imports the failed ones again. When no
OrcaSlicer folder is found beside JusPrin's, the add-printer form offers
"Import from an OrcaSlicer folder…", a folder picker that takes
OrcaSlicer's data folder, its user folder, an account folder or a
machine folder.

OrcaSlicer's PresetBundle::import_presets is unchanged. OrcaImport.cpp
reads each file first and gives a taken name a renamed copy in a temp
folder, so import_presets has nothing to ask; what it reports imported
settles the rest. OrcaSlicer's own files are only read. Detection moves
into the same GUI-free file, with tests.


==== acea861d5a Sign in by email from Home in the --fresh-example harness
After the first launch reaches Home, the agent card signs in by email
against a stand-in JusPrin server on a loopback port: the address, a
wrong code that stays on the code step with four tries left, then the
right code, which brings the account. The harness checks each request
the app sent.


==== c8c2fe4fb1 Send each email sign-in step to the Home page
Home's poll reported a change only when the sign-in phase changed or an
outcome came back. The email steps (code asked for, wrong or expired code,
new code sent, password asked for) all keep the Email phase, so the page
stayed on "busy" after the server answered. The poll now also compares
the email step.

The --fresh-example harness polled the backend itself, which hid this. It
now stops Home's timers and requires the host's poll that brings each step
to send it to the page; without the fix it stalls at
email_sign_in_asks_for_the_code.


==== 83873a6cce Sign in by email through allauth's app API, choosing a code or the password
The email door used to ask the gateway how an address signs in and then
showed either a code step or a password step. The gateway now serves
django-allauth's own API for apps (code/request, code/confirm, login under
ent/jusprin/v2/auth/), so the app speaks allauth's shapes: 401 with a
session token while a code is pending, 200 with the OAuth token in "meta",
400 with an "errors" list, 409 once the pending code is gone. The session
token travels in the X-Session-Token header between the code steps.

After "Continue with email" nothing is sent. The card asks "How do you want
to sign in?": "Email me a 6-digit code" (which also makes the account of a
new address) or a password field with Sign in, plus Forgot password and
Cancel. "Send a new code" always asks for a fresh code instead of allauth's
resend, because a resent code keeps the first deadline and is refused once
the first code is spent. Refusals: wrong code, code no longer works,
too many codes, wrong password, too many tries; anything else ends the
sign-in with one generic error.

Catch2 cases, Vitest and the shell harness's email checks follow the new
steps; the harness's stand-in gateway answers in allauth's shapes. The
canvas boards first-run-12 to 16 draw the steps.


==== df47a0088d Fit the sign-in door into Home's narrow agent card
Home's "Set up the agent" card is about 240 px wide inside. The door was
laid out for the welcome's wider card, so on Home the email field shrank to
about 70 px ("you@ex"), the six 48 px code cells ran past the card's edge,
the link row wrapped with a dot leading the second line, and a spent code's
"Send a new code" wrapped onto two lines. The door's paragraphs also kept the
browser's default margins, because the welcome's margin reset only covers
.onboarding.

Inside .agent-card only: the field and its button stack, each the card's
width; the code cells share the width and stay square; the links drop their
dots and wrap with a gap; a spent code's button takes the width with its
links under it; paragraphs lose their margins. The welcome is unchanged.

Checked by replaying Home states (at rest, choice, code, spent code) into
the built page under Playwright, before and after; canvas board
first-run-10 draws the stacked field.

JusPrin becomes a syndicate of its own on the server, and the server
decides a sign-in's syndicate by its host. So the account provider's
gateway, and the server the account signs in to (derived from it), move

Added 2026-11-01 in ff2fee4fbd on claude/festive-lederberg-693438 (unmerged). `printer_connect` and `printer_connection_status` have only `ToolExposure::Printer`, so MCP answers "This tool is not exposed by JusPrin MCP", despite what [[manual-mcp-tool-repro-recipe]] implies for "any tool".

`JusPrinShellHarness --printer-network-check <dir> <address> <plugin-version> [--simulate-announce]`: copy `plugins/` from the real data folder into `<dir>` first. Without the flag it needs a P1S in cloud mode on; with it, the harness replays the logged announcement into `DeviceManager::on_machine_alive` at 25 s, which tests everything after the plug-in.

Another running JusPrin holding UDP 2021 hides the printer (2026-11-01, same P1S: nothing in 120 s with it running, found in 8 s with it quit), so quit it first (`lsof -nP -iUDP:2021`). Bambu Studio and OrcaSlicer not tried.

The plug-in's `start_discovery` returns success even when the port is held, and it binds UDP 2021 only as the app starts: after the holder lets go, stop + start (with waits, with the sending flag) and `hot_reload_network_plugin()` all left the port empty on 2026-11-01. So the app reports `port_taken` / `not_listening` and asks for a restart; do not retry a recovery without a new idea. Hold the port from a Python socket to test those states.

Port 8883 timing out while the printer announces on UDP (seen 2026-11-01 07:30) is not noise: hearing a printer says nothing about whether it can be logged in to. I wrote this off at the time as "no test of whether a P1S is on", and that same fault then hid behind the "refused" note, see [[bambu-code-minus-one-not-wrong-code]]. To test whether it is on, bind UDP 2021 and listen. To test whether it can be connected, check port 8883 too.

A harness PASS that only checks a note appeared says nothing about whether the note is true. On 2026-11-01 I quoted "in LAN mode, which can be connected" as proof, though only an announcement had been heard.

LAN mode, 2026-11-01: on the same P1S, LAN Only changes the announcement to `DevConnect: lan`, `DevBind: free`. The committed check fails there because it expects cloud mode; those runs used a temporary script. Whether a run starts before the printer is heard depends on the announcement timing (about every 20 s), so check the first "heard" line. A status read that lists the printer suppresses the note by design, so leave it out when testing the note.

Wrong access code, 2026-11-02, P1S firmware 01.10.00.00 in LAN mode, plug-in 02.03.00.62: a connection with a wrong 8-character code made the plug-in answer `ConnectStatusFailed` with msg `-1`, twice, not the `5` upstream's handler treats as a wrong password. So the erase did not run and the wrong code stayed saved. Whether `-1` means the printer refused the code is not known: the plug-in's own log is encrypted (`debug_network_*.log.enc`), TCP 8883 and 990 did accept connections from the same Mac, and a run with the real code has not been done to compare. `5` has never been seen on real hardware.

Announce a project open's result before forgetting its record

Opening a project, starting a new one, or making a calibration test from
outside a calibration project never told its subscribers it had finished: the
model's tool result and the chat's card stayed on Running. Three
agent_bridge_tests cases had failed since 2026-11-03 for this reason.

Since 3aa5a4435d, pump() holds back a call's outcome until the call and the
app's dialogs it answered are done, then announces it. A call that closes its
project also has its record forgotten, because the record belongs to the
project that was closed. That happened inside the call, before pump()
announced it, so when pump() came to announce, the record was gone and nothing
was said. forget_if_closed() assumed the subscribers had already had the
result, which stopped being true with the hold.

forget_if_closed() now leaves the record of the call pump() is running in
place, and pump() forgets it right after announcing it.

Tested: agent_bridge_tests, 554 cases, all pass; before the change, "opening a
project names the activity and reports what was asked", "a calibration test is
made in a calibration project, opening one from any other" and "a calibration
test an MCP client makes after other calls reports what it made" failed.

All tests and harness runs pass, and the connection-skill checks ran against the real P1S. Nothing is pushed; jusprin-newui is 8 commits ahead of GitHub.

content.text:
The sign-in, credits and first-run work is now on jusprin-newui, squashed from 19 commits into four. The three failing C++ tests had one shared bug, which I fixed, and they pass now. The `--printer-connect-skill` checks pass against your real P1S and for someone with no Bambu plug-in. All of it is committed locally, and nothing is pushed.

**What's now on jusprin-newui**

That work was the only big branch not yet merged. Most other old branches were already in under different commit names. The session that owned it said it was finished and asked me to merge it. jusprin-newui now ends with these commits:

1. Add JusPrin Cloud credits (balances, prices, the low-balance notice, print-report rewards)
2. First launch: Welcome, then Printers, then Home
3. Sign in by email from the welcome and Home, and show what an OrcaSlicer import brought
4. Sign in to jusprinv2.obico.io, and send Continue with Google straight to Google
5. Fit the first-launch printer form and its test to today's printer chat and cards
6. Announce a project open's result before forgetting its record
7. Drop OrcaSlicer's name from a dialog log line the wording guard reads

The squashed result has exactly the same files as the original branch plus jusprin-newui's own changes. The only exceptions are the printer card and its styles, where the first-run "assumed" printer mark now sits on today's full card.

**What the merge needed**

- **The add-printer form didn't build.** The first-launch form hosts a printer chat, and that chat's host interface gained five methods after the branch was cut.
- **One Home page test still looked for the one-line printer chip**, which today's cards no longer have.
- **A guard failure that was already there:** the Agent page check that keeps OrcaSlicer's name out of text the model reads was failing on a log line. That line never reaches the model, so I reworded it.

**The three failing tests**

When the agent opened a project, started a new one, or made a calibration test outside a calibration project, the call never said it had finished. Its card and the model's tool result stayed on "Running". Since Nov 3, the app holds back a finished call's announcement until the dialogs the call answered are done. A call that closes its project also deletes its own record, because the record belongs to the closed project, and that happened before the held announcement went out. Now the record is deleted right after the announcement. I saw all three tests fail before the change and pass after it.

**Test results**

- **C++ suites, all pass:** agent bridge 554, JusPrin 222, workspace 51, brand 49.
- **Page tests, all pass:** Home page 154, Agent page 666.
- **Shell harness, which drives the real app:**
  - default run: 600 checks pass
  - first launch with email sign-in: 51 checks pass
  - connection skill against your P1S: 79 checks pass, with no message sent to the printer
  - connection skill with no plug-in: 74 checks pass

**Before you push**

- **Sign-in won't work on production builds yet.** Builds now sign in at jusprinv2.obico.io, and that production host doesn't answer yet; staging does. Until production is live, a build from jusprin-newui can only sign in when `JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT` points at staging.
- **Left as they were:** the P1S direct-connect harness mode, which you asked to keep uncommitted, is still uncommitted in `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`. The original branch, `claude/elated-sutherland-84a741`, is untouched.
Do you need to further squash the fix for the failing cases?

I'd squash one of the three fix commits, not all three.

**The one I'd squash.** "Fit the first-launch printer form and its test to today's printer chat and cards" repairs the "First launch: Welcome, then Printers, then Home" commit. The add-printer form and the Home page test both come from that commit. As the history stands, that commit and the two sign-in commits after it don't build, because the form is missing the five methods the printer chat's host now requires. A `git bisect` that lands on any of those three commits would hit a build error that has nothing to do with the bug being chased. Folding the fix into the first-launch commit makes every commit build.

**The two I'd keep separate.**

- **The fix for the three failing tests** ("Announce a project open's result before forgetting its record") is a bug from 3aa5a4435d, the Nov 3 commit that holds back a call's announcement. It's unrelated to the sign-in work. As its own commit it's easy to find, and easy to revert if needed.
- **The wording fix** for the log line also predates the merge. It's a one-line change that's clear on its own.

Decision needed: should I fold the first-launch fix into the first-launch commit? This rewrites five local commits that haven't been pushed: the first-launch commit and the four after it. The result would be six commits on top of today's printer card commit: four feature commits, then the two standalone fixes. The final files stay byte for byte the same, and I'd check that before and after. The cost is a rebase of unpushed history, which is why I'm asking rather than doing it. The other option is to leave the history as it is, with three commits that don't build. My pick is to fold it in. Shall I?
Any reason why we shouldn't squash all of them into one?

Yes, two reasons, though only one of them is strong.

**The strong reason: the fix for the three failing tests should stay separate.** It fixes a bug from Nov 3 that has nothing to do with sign-in. In one big commit, it gets reverted along with everything else, and that's a real possibility right now: builds sign in at jusprinv2.obico.io, and that host doesn't answer in production yet. If you have to back out the sign-in work before production is ready, reverting one combined commit would also bring back the bug where opening a project leaves the agent's call stuck on "Running". A separate commit also makes the fix easy to copy to another branch, such as main or a release.

**The weaker reason: a commit that big is hard to search.** One commit would cover about 120 files and 8,000 lines. `git bisect` or `git blame` would land on it and tell you little about which change caused a problem. Recent history doesn't hold to small commits, though. 83a8431df2 combined three changes to the printer chat into one commit. So splitting the sign-in work into four is my preference, not a rule this branch follows.

Squashing the sign-in work into one commit is fine. The four commits plus the first-launch fix can become a single commit, and nothing breaks. The wording fix is one line, and it can ride along with either commit.

Decision needed: how should these local commits be squashed before pushing? All of them are unpushed, and any of these options rewrites them with the final files byte for byte the same. Option one is a single commit for everything, the simplest log, which you'd lose the test fix with if you reverted the sign-in work. Option two is two commits: one for the sign-in, credits and first-run work with its first-launch fix and the wording fix, and one for the fix to the three failing tests. Option three is what I proposed before: four feature commits plus the two fixes. My pick is two commits, because it keeps the test fix safe from a sign-in revert and still gives a clean log. Which do you want?

go with what you've suggested.

---
name: git-checkout-no-paths-moves-head
description: "Building a tree in a temp GIT_INDEX_FILE: never run `git checkout <commit> --` with no paths; it detaches HEAD and rewrites the working tree"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-11-05, while building a commit tree with GIT_INDEX_FILE set, a stray `git checkout b75705cd59 --` (no paths) detached HEAD in the main checkout and rewrote three working-tree files; the branch ref and the real index were untouched. Recovered with `git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/<branch>` then `git checkout -- <those files>` from the real index.

**Why:** the main checkout holds other sessions' uncommitted work; a moved HEAD or a hard reset there can destroy it.

**How to apply:** build trees only with read-tree, `update-index --cacheinfo` and write-tree inside the temp index, then commit-tree and `update-ref <ref> <new> <old>`. Check `.git/HEAD` and `git status` after any plumbing run. See [[restore-temp-edits-from-a-copy]].
